lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Vocabulary Worksheet — Unit 1: Education
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to talk and write about their own studies and plans using vocabulary items related to schooling.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. Displays the worksheet pictures and asks Ss to guess the topic.
Ss. Guess the topic: studies, university, studying abroad...
T. Introduces Leila, a student in Taha Hussein high school, and her plans.
T. Asks Ss to read "Leila's plans" for gist: Where does Leila want to continue her studies?
Ss. Read and answer: Abroad, in a foreign country.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. Underline graduate, degree, abroad, research, scholarship, timetable individually (Think).
Ss. Compare with a partner and guess the meanings from context (Pair).
Ss. Report to the class (Share).
T. Writes the words on the board, grouped by meaning: school life (timetable) · finishing studies (graduate, degree) · studying far away (abroad, scholarship, research).
T. Elicits and confirms each meaning through the context, models each word, and Ss repeat chorally and individually.
T. Highlights form: graduate from + school; go / study abroad (no "to"); research is uncountable (do research, not *researches).

stages.name: Remember
steps: T. Sets Exercise A: Match each word with its meaning.
Ss. Do the task individually.
T. Sets Exercise B: Complete the sentences with the target words from the word bank.
Ss. Do the task individually.
T. Monitors, noting typical errors.
Ss. Peer-check.
T. Checks answers as a class. Key A: 1 c · 2 f · 3 e · 4 a · 5 b · 6 d
T. Checks answers as a class. Key B: 1 graduate · 2 timetable · 3 scholarship · 4 degree · 5 research · 6 abroad
T. Corrects errors and re-drills graduate, scholarship, abroad, research.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. Sets Exercise C: Odd one out.
T. ICQ: Do you circle the word that belongs or cross out the word that doesn't?
Ss. Cross out the word that doesn't belong.
Ss. Do the task individually.
Ss. Justify their choices to a partner.
T. Gives the expected answers. Key C: 1 break · 2 scholarship · 3 timetable · 4 research
T. Sets Exercise D: Words that go together, and models a sentence: I want to study abroad after the Bac.
Ss. Write one sentence per verb.
Ss. Check a partner's sentences.

T. Gives the expected collocations: do research / homework / an experiment · get a degree / a scholarship / good marks · study abroad / hard / a subject · take an exam / notes / a break · pass an exam / a test / a course

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. Presents the Production task: write three sentences about your studies using the target words.
Ss. Write their three sentences.

T. Writes the speaking prompts on the board (teacher-added): What will you do after you graduate? Would you like to study abroad? Where? What degree do you want to get? Do you need a scholarship? Why?
Ss. Interview each other in pairs.
T. Monitors without interrupting and notes good language and errors.
Ss. Report on their partner.
Teacher: Youssef Nejjar

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 1 Education — Functions: Opinions, Agreeing & Disagreeing
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express their opinions about school issues and agree or disagree politely, using: "In my opinion… / I think… / I agree. / You're right. / I don't agree. / I see your point, but…"

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Do you like homework? How much homework do you do every day?”
Ss. answer freely.
T. reads / plays the dialogue and sets the gist question: Who is for homework every day? Who is against?
Ss. listen, read and answer (for: Salma — against: Yassine, Hind).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: T. asks Ss to find the expressions in the dialogue and classify them.
Ss. complete Task A (opinion / agreeing / disagreeing) individually, then compare in pairs.
T. checks meaning with CCQs: “I see your point, but…” — Does she agree 100%? (No.) Is it polite? (Yes.)
T. drills stress and intonation: “I don't think so!”, “Exactly!”, “You're right.” — Ss. repeat chorally and individually.

stages.name: Remember
steps: T. explains Task B and the expression box.
Ss. complete the mini-dialogues individually, then check in pairs.
Ss. read the dialogues aloud in pairs; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models statement 1 of Task C with a strong student.
Ss. react to each statement in pairs (agree / disagree / give an opinion + a reason) and write their exchange.
T. monitors; 3–4 pairs act out their exchanges.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. sets the situation: a class council must choose ONE project — a computer room or a school bus.
Ss. read their role cards (Task D), note ideas (2 min), then role-play and reach a decision.
2–3 pairs perform; the class votes.
T. gives delayed feedback on the errors noted (e.g. *I am agree).

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 1 Education — Reading: Why Do Children Leave School?
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to show understanding of the text "Why Do Children Leave School?" by getting the main idea of each paragraph, understanding details and giving their opinion about solutions.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. shows the four pictures and asks: What problem does the text talk about? Why do some children leave school?
Ss. brainstorm reasons in pairs; T. writes them on the board and pre-teaches poverty, countryside, diploma.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Skimming: Ss. read quickly (2 min) and tick the best title (Task A); T. checks the predictions on the board.
Scanning: Ss. decide true or false and justify with a quote (Task B); pairs compare
Main ideas: Ss. write the main idea of paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 and answer the interpretation question (Task C). T. checks.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. discuss in groups: What is the best way to stop school dropout in your region? Each group agrees on two ideas.
Ss. write their view (Task D); group reporters share; the class votes on the best idea.
Interaction: Group / Ind. · Material: Worksheet – Task D

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 1 Education — Grammar: The Simple Past
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to talk about school experiences in the past using the simple past tense (regular and irregular verbs, was / were, didn't, Did…?)
lessons.point: • Regular verbs: verb + -ed → walked, loved, studied, stopped. • Irregular verbs: learn them by heart → go → went, have → had, write → wrote.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures (a louh, a village school in the 1960s) and asks: “Where did your grandparents go to school?”
Ss. read Salma's text about her grandfather and answer: Did Hajj Ahmed go to high school? Why?
Ss. underline the verbs in the past.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: T. writes two examples on the board: He walked to school. / He went to the msid. — CCQs: Now or in the past? (Past.) Is it finished? (Yes.)
Ss. complete the table (Task A: regular, irregular, be) guided by line 1.
T. elicits the rules and completes the Remember box with Ss (-ed; did / didn't + base verb; was / were).
T. drills the three -ed sounds: /t/ walked, /d/ loved, /ɪd/ started.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in the simple past (Task B) individually.
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board and focuses on irregular verbs.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. transform the sentences into the negative and yes / no questions (Task C).
Ss. ask and answer the questions in pairs with short answers (Yes, he did. / No, they weren't.).

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about their first year at primary school (Task D).
In pairs, Ss. read their sentences and ask one follow-up question (Did you…?).
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback (*didn't went, *Did you went).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 1 Education — Grammar: Reflexive Pronouns
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to talk about their school life using reflexive pronouns (myself … themselves; by + myself).
lessons.point: • Use a reflexive pronoun when the subject and the object are the same person: He hurt himself.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures and asks: “Would you like to study at a boarding school? Why / why not?”
Ss. read Hind's text and answer: How did Hind feel at the end of the week?
Ss. circle the words ending in -self / -selves.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: T. mimes “I look at myself in the mirror” — CCQs: Who do I look at? (Me.) Same person? (Yes.)
Ss. complete the table (Task A) and find an example for each pronoun in the text.
T. elicits the rules (Remember box): subject = object; -self / -selves; by + myself = alone; emphasis.
T. drills stress: mySELF, ourSELVES, themSELVES.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the correct reflexive pronoun (Task B).
Pairs check; T. corrects and highlights common errors (*hisself, *theirselves).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. goes through the example in Task C (Nobody helped me… → I did it by myself.).
Ss. rewrite the sentences with by + reflexive pronoun and make a simple past question.
Ss. ask and answer the questions in pairs.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five true sentences about their school life using the prompts (Task D).
Ss. share in groups of three; each group chooses the most interesting sentence for the class.
T. gives feedback on pronoun and past-tense errors.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 1 Education — Writing: A Postcard
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a postcard from a summer camp, with the correct layout, the simple past and expressing an opinion while respecting mechanics.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. shows the pictures of Ifrane and asks: Do people still send postcards? Who to?
Ss. read Salma's postcard and answer: Who is she writing to? Where is she?
Ss. label the parts of the postcard (Task A); T. checks and highlights layout (address on the right).

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put Yassine's postcard in the right order (Task B).
Ss. rewrite the sentences with capitals and punctuation (Task C); T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. sets the situation: you are on a school trip or at a summer camp in a Moroccan city.
Ss. plan their postcard with the sentence starters (Task D); pairs share their plans and add one idea.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their postcard in the frame (Task E).
Ss. check their text with the checklist, then swap with a partner for peer checking.
T. collects the postcards to mark with the marking guide.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Vocabulary (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to understand and use vocabulary related to the generation gap and social problems (childhood, adolescence, generation gap, autonomy, tolerance, homeless, jobless) to talk about society in the past and today.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. writes “Society: then and now” on the board and asks: “Who lives with their grandparents? What is different between your life and theirs?”
Ss. share ideas; T. writes key ideas on the board.
T. shows the three pictures; Ss. describe them.
Ss. read Salma's text twice and answer: “What worries Salma's grandfather?” (jobless graduates, homeless people).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the seven words with their definitions (Task A), then compare answers with a partner.
T. checks orally and refers Ss. back to the highlighted words in the text.

T. checks meaning with CCQs: “Is a homeless person without a job or without a house? (a house)” · “Childhood or adolescence: 15 years old? (adolescence)” · “Autonomy: do you decide or do your parents decide? (I decide)”.
T. shows the suffix -less in homeless / jobless (= without).
Pronunciation: stress in adolescence (ooOo), autonomy (oOoo), tolerance (Ooo); choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the seven sentences with words from the box (Task B).
T. corrects; Ss. read the sentences aloud.
Ss. cross out the odd word in each line (Task C) and justify orally: “homeless — it isn't a period of life.”

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models the first sentence about himself: “The best memory of my childhood is …”.
Ss. complete the five personal sentences (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who asks one follow-up question.
T. invites 3–4 Ss. to share and corrects word use.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write 4–5 sentences comparing teenagers' life in their grandparents' time and today, using at least four new words (Production).
Ss. read their sentences to the class; classmates count the new words used.
T. gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Functions: complaining (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to recognise and use expressions for complaining and for responding to a complaint, identify speakers' opinions in a short reading dialogue and transfer information from what they read.
lessons.point: Complaining: I'm fed up with / sick and tired of + noun / -ing · I'd like to complain about + noun · It's not good enough! · I'm afraid I have to say …

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “What makes people angry in a neighbourhood?”
Ss. tick three problems they expect to read about (Task A).
Ss. read the short radio dialogue “Your Voice” silently once, check their predictions and complete the table: caller, city, complaint, opinion (Task B).
Ss. compare answers with a partner.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. read the dialogue again and write the name of the speaker who has each opinion (Task C).
T. checks answers and asks: “Which phrases show an opinion?” (In my opinion, I think, I believe …).
Ss. scan the dialogue and complete the extracts, then mark them C (complaining) or R (responding) (Task D).
T. builds the board: Complaining / Responding (Remember box).
Form: fed up with / sick and tired of + noun or -ing; complain about + noun.
Pronunciation: stress on key words and falling intonation for strong feelings: “I'm SICK and TIRED of it!”; choral and individual drilling; Ss. read the extracts aloud.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the four mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task E).
T. corrects; Ss. read the dialogues aloud with the right intonation.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a complaint and a response for each situation (Task F), then practise them with a partner.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says which expressions they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task G). Ss. prepare for one minute without writing full sentences.
Ss. role-play the neighbour situation, then swap roles.
Two pairs perform for the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on expressions and intonation.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Reading (PDP)
lessons.topic: Then and now: a grandfather remembers
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to predict the content of a text on social issues and check their predictions, read for specific information and inference, and associate words with ideas in the text.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks: “How was life different when your grandparents were young?” and writes Ss.' ideas on the board.
T. pre-teaches obey, graduate, solidarity and lonely with pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the pictures and tick the ideas they expect in the text (Task A).

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text in two minutes and check their predictions in Task A.
Ss. choose the best title (Task B); T. asks which words helped them.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying from the text (Task C).
T. checks; Ss. read the justification aloud.
Ss. answer the questions (Task D), including the inference question: “What does he mean by ‘Every generation has its problems’?”
Ss. find words in the text associated with values of the past, social problems today and modern life (Task E).
T. collects the words in three columns on the board.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: T. asks: “Do you agree with Hajj Driss? Was life better in the past?”
Ss. write 3–4 sentences giving their opinion (Task F).
Ss. compare their opinions with a partner, then 3–4 Ss. share with the class.
T. links the ideas to the next lessons: used to and writing about past habits.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Grammar Part 1: used to (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use used to and didn't use to to talk about past habits and states that are no longer true, and ask questions with Did … use to …?
lessons.point: used to + base form = a past habit or state that is not true now: I used to get up at dawn. (now I don't)

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows a picture of himself as a child and says: “I used to play football in the street every day. Now I don't.”
Ss. look at the two pictures and say what is different.
Ss. read the dialogue between Salma and Grandma Rkia and answer: “What did Grandma use to do every day?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline used to in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
T. checks and draws a timeline: past ✕✕✕✕ | now ✗.
CCQs: “Does Grandma fetch water now? (No) Did she do it once or many times? (many times)”.
T. highlights didn't use to / Did … use to …? and the pronunciation /ˈjuːstə/ (Remember box); choral drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the eight sentences with the correct form of used to and the verb (Task B).
T. corrects on the board, focusing on use after did / didn't.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. does the example about Mr. Bennani.
Ss. write then-and-now sentences from the table (Task C).
Ss. read their sentences aloud; T. corrects.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four true sentences about their childhood with used to / didn't use to (Task D).
Ss. interview a partner with Did you use to …? questions and report: “Nadia used to …, but she didn't use to …”.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Grammar Part 2: articles (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the articles a, an and the, and no article, correctly when they talk and write about people and places in their community.
lessons.point: a + consonant sound: a bed, a university /j/, a European city · an + vowel sound: an old man, an hour (silent h), an honest girl

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Have you ever helped people in need? Is there an association in your town?”
Ss. look at the two pictures and guess the place.
Ss. read Salma's diary and answer: “Where did Salma and Yassine go? Who did they help?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find examples of each use in the text and complete the table (Task A).
T. checks answers on the board.
CCQs: “‘a shelter’ — do we know it already? (No) ‘The shelter’ — which one? (the one in the medina) ‘Homeless people’ — specific or in general? (in general)”.
T. presents a + consonant sound / an + vowel sound (an hour, a university) and the uses of the and Ø (Remember box).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with a, an, the or Ø (Task B).
T. corrects and asks Ss. to justify each answer.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the text about the association in Fes (Task C).
Ss. explain their choices to a partner: first mention, job, general or specific.
T. checks with the whole class.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write 5–6 sentences about a person or an association that helps people in their town, and underline the articles (Task D).
Ss. exchange papers and check the articles; 2–3 Ss. read their sentences aloud.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 2 - Society — Writing: past habits (Product approach)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a well-organised paragraph of 100–120 words about past habits, with a topic sentence, supporting ideas, connectors and a concluding sentence.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss. of Hajj Driss's interview and asks: “What did people use to do in the past?”
Ss. read Salma's model paragraph and say what it is about.
Ss. write the number of each part in the boxes (topic sentence, supporting idea, concluding sentence) and circle the connectors (Task A).
T. checks and shows the paragraph plan on the board.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put Karim's paragraph in the right order (Task B) and explain which words helped them.
Ss. complete the sentences with the connectors in the box (Task C).
T. corrects and stresses the comma after each connector.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. presents the topic: “How life used to be when my parents or grandparents were young.”
Ss. brainstorm ideas together; T. writes useful verbs on the board.
Ss. complete the outline with notes, using the sentence starters (Task D).
T. monitors and helps Ss. choose three supporting ideas.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their paragraph of 100–120 words with a title (Task E).
Ss. check their paragraph with the checklist and correct their mistakes.
T. collects the paragraphs for marking with the marking guide.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Vocabulary: Health, illness & fitness (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use lexis related to health, diseases, fitness and medicine to describe health problems, treatments and healthy habits.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “When was the last time you were ill? What did you do?” and elicits a few words (ill, doctor, medicine).
T. displays the four pictures; Ss. say what they can see.
Ss. read Yassine’s blog post and answer the gist question: “Why did he go to the health centre?” (he had the flu).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and asks CCQs: “Is flu a symptom or an illness?” “Can you buy these tablets without a prescription?”
Ss. classify the words in the box into the four columns (Task B).
T. drills the pronunciation and word stress: cough /kɒf/, throat, disease, prescription (oOo), obesity (oOoo).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words from the text (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; volunteers read the sentences aloud and T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. presents the collocations in the box: catch a cold, take medicine, keep fit, go on a diet, see a doctor, have a check-up.
Ss. complete the sentences about themselves (Task D), then read them to a partner, who asks one follow-up question.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write a short message to a cousin who is often ill, with tips to stay healthy, using at least six words from the lesson (Task E).
2–3 Ss. read their messages; the class counts the target words used.
T. gives delayed feedback on collocation errors (e.g. *take a cold → catch a cold).

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Functions: Seeking & giving advice (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to seek and give advice and talk about health problems in short conversations, and identify a speaker’s attitude and specific information in a listening text.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. mimes a headache and asks: “What’s the matter with me? What should I do?” Ss. suggest ideas.
T. displays the pictures and asks: “Where is Salma? How does she feel?”
Ss. listen to Salma and the school nurse and complete the nurse’s card (Task A).
Ss. listen again and tick the speakers’ attitude (Task B), then justify with the words or tone they heard.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. read the dialogue between Yassine and Imane and answer: “What are Yassine’s problems? What advice does Imane give?”
Ss. find the expressions and write them in the right column (Task C); T. builds the board: health problems / asking for advice / giving advice / responding.
CCQs: “‘You’d better see a doctor’ — is it strong or weak advice?” “Does ‘If I were you’ talk about me or you?”
Form & pronunciation: should + base verb, Why don’t you …?, If I were you, I’d …; silent l in should; stress and sympathetic falling tone (I’m SOrry to HEAR that). Choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task D).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs read the dialogue aloud; T. re-drills difficult lines.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write and practise a short exchange for each situation (Task E): ask about the problem, then give advice. They swap roles.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says which expression they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task F). Ss. role-play a friend with a health problem and a friend who gives at least three pieces of advice, without looking at the dialogue.
Ss. swap roles and choose a new problem.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Reading: Healthy teens, happy teens (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use reading strategies (predicting, skimming, scanning and guessing from context) to understand a text about teenage health, take notes and summarise it.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “How many hours do you sleep? What do you eat for breakfast?” and writes key words on the board.
T. pre-teaches concentrate, tooth decay and anxious with examples and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. read the text quickly to check their predictions (Task A).
Ss. skim the first lines of each paragraph and tick the main idea of the text (Task B).
Ss. scan the text and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task C). Pair check; feedback with the paragraph numbers.
Ss. guess the meaning of the words and the expression from context (Task D). T. asks: “Which words around it helped you?”
T. shows how to take notes (key words, no full sentences).
Ss. take notes on the doctor’s advice for each key (Task E), then compare with a partner.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. use their notes to write a 4–5 sentence summary of the text (Task F), starting with the given sentence.
Ss. exchange summaries and check that the four keys are there; 2–3 Ss. read theirs to the class.
T. links to the Writing lesson: “What problem would you write to Dr. Idrissi about?”

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Grammar Part 1: Modals (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the modals should / shouldn’t, must / have to, mustn’t / don’t have to and may / might / could to express advice, obligation, prohibition and possibility about health.
lessons.point: Modal + base verb: You should rest. ✓ You should to rest ✗ · She musts ✗ → She must / She has to · Questions: Should I …? / Do I have to …?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. displays the two pictures and asks: “What happened to Hamza? Where is he now?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “What’s wrong with Hamza? Can he play in the final?”
T. checks the answers and writes four sentences from the dialogue on the board.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the modals in the dialogue and complete the table with the function and an example (Task A); pair check.
T. elicits the rules from the Remember box: modal + base verb, questions with Should I …? / Do I have to …?
CCQs: “‘You mustn’t walk’ — can he walk?” “‘You don’t have to stay’ — is it necessary?” “‘It might be a sprain’ — is the doctor sure?” Pronunciation: mustn’t, have to.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct modal in each sentence (Task B).
Ss. compare in pairs; T. corrects on the board and asks Ss. to say why (advice, obligation, prohibition or possibility).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1: “Omar should see a dentist.”
Ss. write a sentence for each situation with the modal given (Task C), then read them to a partner, who checks the meaning.
Volunteers write their sentences on the board for class correction.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write six rules and tips for a “healthy school charter” with must / have to, mustn’t, don’t have to, should / shouldn’t and one sentence with might (Task D).
Ss. compare charters with a partner and choose the three best rules for a class poster.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*should to, *musts, mustn’t vs don’t have to).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Grammar Part 2: The present perfect (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the present perfect with for, since, ever, never, just, already and yet to talk about recent changes and experiences related to health.
lessons.point: have / has + past participle (regular: stop → stopped; irregular: go → gone, eat → eaten, lose → lost, feel → felt, have → had)

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. reminds Ss of Yassine’s problem (Reading / Functions lessons): “Remember Yassine? He was always tired. What should he do?”
Ss. read Yassine’s message to Imane and answer: “What has he changed?”
T. checks and writes three sentences on the board: I’ve joined the team. I haven’t eaten crisps for a month. Have you ever tried yoga?

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the present perfect in the message and complete the form table (Task A).
T. elicits the form: have / has + past participle; short answers; regular and irregular participles (gone, eaten, lost, felt).
Ss. find the time words in the message and complete their meaning (Task A — time words).
CCQs: “‘I’ve joined the team’ — is he in the team now?” “‘for six weeks’ — when did he start?” Pronunciation: weak forms I’ve, has, Have you ever …?

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in brackets in the present perfect (Task B), paying attention to the position of never, just and already.
Pair check; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with for, since, ever, never, already or yet (Task C).
T. draws a timeline for for / since; Ss. justify their answers.
Ss. write two true sentences about themselves with for and since and read them to a partner.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write a short message to a friend about what they have / haven’t done this year to stay healthy, with one Have you ever …? question (Task D).
Ss. exchange messages and answer their partner’s question in writing.
T. gives delayed feedback on errors (*I have stop, *since two months, present perfect with yesterday).

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Writing: A letter asking for advice (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a letter asking for advice about a health problem, using the layout of a letter, connectors and expressions for describing a problem and asking for advice.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Dr. Idrissi’s article (Reading lesson): “Who is Dr. Idrissi? Why do students write to her?”
Ss. read Yassine’s letter and answer: “What is his problem? What does he ask?”

Ss. number the eight parts of the letter (Task A); T. checks and highlights the fixed phrases: Dear Dr. …, I am writing to ask for your advice …, What do you think I should do?, I look forward to hearing from you., Yours sincerely,

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. complete the useful expressions with the words in the box (Task B); pair check.
Ss. join the sentences with because, so, but and also (Task C). T. elicits the punctuation rules (comma before so and but).

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. choose a health problem from the box and plan their letter in the outline (Task D): introduction, the problem, what I have tried, asking for advice, closing — notes only.
Ss. turn their notes into sentences with the sentence starters, then compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps with the present perfect and should.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their full letter to Dr. Idrissi (100–120 words) in the letter frame (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the self-assessment checklist and correct it. T. collects the letters for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Vocabulary: Waste, energy, pollution & recycling (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use vocabulary related to waste, energy, pollution and recycling to describe environmental problems and solutions in their town.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the four pictures and asks: “What can you see? Which pictures show a problem? Which show a solution?”
Ss. answer with the words they know; T. writes them on the board.
Ss. read Salma's post and answer the gist question: “What are the two problems in Agadir? What does the Green Club do?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the six words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and builds a word map on the board: Waste / Energy / Pollution / Recycling.
CCQs: “Is a plastic bottle on the beach litter? (Yes) Can we use the sun again tomorrow? (Yes — it is renewable) Is oil renewable? (No — a fossil fuel)”.
Pronunciation: stress in pollute / pollution, recycle, environment; waste = waist; choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; volunteers read the sentences aloud; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. classify the twelve words in the table (Task C) and justify one choice to a partner.
Ss. complete the word-building table and the three sentences (Task D).
T. highlights the suffixes -tion, -able, -ful and checks with a dictionary.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four sentences about environmental problems in their town and what people can do (Task E), using at least four new words.
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who suggests one more solution.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Functions: Making & responding to suggestions (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to make suggestions and accept or refuse them politely when planning actions to protect the environment.
lessons.point: Let's + base verb · Why don't we / you + base verb? · Shall we + base verb? · We could + base verb

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures; Ss. answer the questions and predict the topic of the interview (Task A).
Ss. listen to the radio interview and tick the main topic (Task B).
Ss. listen again and complete the fact file (Task C); pair check.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen a third time and say who uses each expression (Task D).
Ss. read the tapescript and classify the expressions: making / accepting / refusing (Task E). T. builds the board.
T. focuses on form with the Remember box: Let's / Why don't we / Shall we + base verb; How about / I suggest + -ing.
CCQs: “Is ‘I'm afraid I can't’ a yes or a no? (No — polite) After ‘How about’, do we say ‘to bring’ or ‘bringing’? (bringing)”.
Pronunciation: stress on the key word and friendly intonation; choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the dialogue between Hiba and Ilyas with the expressions in the box (Task F).
Ss. check in pairs; two pairs read the dialogue aloud; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models problem 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a suggestion for each problem and their partner's answer, using a different expression each time (Task G), then swap roles.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says which expressions they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task H). Ss. role-play planning World Environment Day without looking at the dialogue and agree on a plan.
Pairs present their plan to the class; the class votes for the best idea.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Reading: Can we still save our coast? (PDP)
lessons.topic: Can we still save our coast?
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to identify the main idea of each paragraph and specific details in an article about environmental problems, and suggest solutions to a local problem.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “What did you see on the beach last summer? Is our town clean?”
T. pre-teaches drought, ban, tiny, rare with the pictures and examples.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the article in two minutes to check their predictions (Task A), then match each paragraph with its main idea (Task B). Pair check; feedback with the key words.
Ss. scan the text to decide if the statements are true or false and correct the false ones (Task C). Volunteers read the lines that justify their answers.
Ss. find what the underlined words refer to and the words with the given meanings (Task D). T. shows how the context helps.
Ss. complete the problem–solution table with information from the text (Task E); T. builds the table on the board.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. choose a problem in their town, describe it and suggest two solutions (Task F).
In groups, Ss. compare their solutions and choose the best one; one S. per group reports to the class.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Grammar Part 1: Too & enough (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use too, too much / too many and (not) enough correctly to describe environmental problems in their school and town.
lessons.point: too goes before the adjective: too hot · enough goes after the adjective but before the noun: warm enough / enough water

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Can you swim in this river? Why not? Is there space for more rubbish in the bin?”
Ss. answer freely; T. recasts: “It's too dirty to swim in.”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer the gist question: “What problems did the Green Club find?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the highlighted phrases and complete the table with examples from the dialogue (Task A); pair check.
T. builds the rules on the board.
CCQs: “The water is too cold. Can we swim? (No) Is ‘too’ the same as ‘very’? (No — too has a negative result) Before or after the adjective does ‘enough’ go? (after) And with a noun? (before)”.
T. uses the Remember box; pronunciation: weak form /tə/ in “too dirty to swim”.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with too, too much, too many or enough (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board and asks Ss to justify each choice.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models the example on the board.
Ss. join the sentences with too … to or (not) … enough to (Task C), then compare with a partner.
Volunteers write their sentences on the board; the class corrects them.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four sentences about real problems in their school or town with too, too much / many and (not) enough (Task D).
In groups, Ss. compare their sentences and choose the biggest problem; one S. reports it to the class.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Grammar Part 2: Prepositions after adjectives & verbs (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the correct prepositions after common adjectives and verbs to talk about environmental problems and their own actions.
lessons.point: Some adjectives and verbs always take the same preposition — learn them together: afraid of · proud of · famous for · rich in · harmful to · think about · care about · result in

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “What are the students doing? Why is the field dry?”
Ss. read Khadija's club report and answer the gist question: “What did the students do last month?” (They took part in a tree-planting day.)

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the highlighted phrases and classify them: adjective + preposition / verb + preposition / verb + object + preposition (Task A); pair check. T. builds the table on the board.
CCQs: “Can we say ‘interested by’? (No — interested in) What comes after a preposition: recycle or recycling? (recycling)”.
T. presents the extra phrases in the Remember box; pronunciation: weak forms /əv/, /tə/, /fə/ in connected speech.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the right preposition (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board and Ss. repeat the full phrases.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the four questions with a preposition (Task C).
Ss. interview a partner and note the answers, then report one answer to the class: “Salma is worried about …”.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write a short paragraph about themselves and the environment using at least five phrases (Task D).
Ss. read their paragraphs in groups; the group chooses the most interesting one.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Writing: An opinion paragraph (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write an opinion paragraph that describes an environmental problem in their town, gives reasons and examples, and suggests a solution.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Anas's article (Reading lesson): “What can each of us do for the environment?”
Ss. read Anas's paragraph and answer: “What is his opinion? Give one of his examples.”
Ss. label the five parts of the paragraph (Task A); T. checks and highlights the opinion phrases and connectors: In my opinion, Firstly, Secondly, Moreover, In conclusion.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. complete the paragraph about a car-free medina with the connectors in the box (Task B); pair check.
Ss. rewrite the sentences with capital letters, commas, full stops and apostrophes (Task C). T. stresses the comma after connectors.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. brainstorm environmental problems in their town in pairs; T. collects ideas on the board (litter, polluted river, traffic, wasting water …).
Ss. choose one problem and plan their paragraph in the outline (Task D): topic sentence · two reasons / effects · solution · conclusion — notes only.
Ss. turn the notes into sentences with the sentence starters, then compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their opinion paragraph (100–120 words) in the frame (Task E).
Ss. check their paragraph with the self-assessment checklist and correct it. T. collects the paragraphs for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Vocabulary: Free time & entertainment (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words related to leisure and recreational activities to talk about their free time, and guess the meaning of unfamiliar words from context and word parts.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “What did you do last weekend? Is free time important for you?” and writes Ss' activities on the board.
T. displays the four pictures; Ss. name the activities.
Ss. read Yassir's blog post and answer the gist question: “What does Yassir do in his free time?” (hiking, chess, board games, cinema).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the highlighted words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and drills the words for stress: PAStime, AUdience, enterTAINment, LEIsure.
T. presents the strategy box: context, word parts, part of speech, dictionary last.
Ss. guess the meaning of the words in bold and write the clue (Task B); T. elicits the clues.
T. asks CCQs: “Is a couch potato active? (No) If you take up a hobby, is it new or old? (new)”.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the word family table (Task C) and check spelling with the dictionary.
T. corrects on the board and highlights the suffixes -ment, -ion, -ing, -able.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task D), changing the form where needed (hang out → hung out).
Ss. check in pairs; T. elicits answers and gives feedback.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about their own free time using at least five new words (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner and find one activity they both enjoy; 2–3 Ss. report to the class.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on word form and stress.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Functions: Expressing interest & indifference (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express interest, indifference and lack of interest in leisure activities, and react to other people's preferences with appropriate intonation.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Who is Anas? What is a school radio?”
Ss. predict the four activities Anas talks about (Task A).
Ss. listen to the interview and check their predictions (Task A).
Ss. listen again and choose the main idea (Task B); T. elicits the answer.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen for the last time and write the expressions in the right column (Task C), then compare with a partner.
T. builds the board: Strong interest / Indifference / No interest, with the prepositions keen on, crazy about, fascinated by, interested in.
T. asks CCQs: “Does Anas want to play football? (not really) Is ‘I don't mind’ positive or neutral? (neutral)”.
T. models lively falling intonation for interest and a flat tone for indifference (Say it right box); choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-exchanges with the expressions in the box (Task D).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs read the exchanges aloud with the right intonation.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models one line: “Going to the theatre? I'm really keen on it because …”.
Ss. write a reaction and a reason for each activity (Task E), then compare with a partner: “Me too!” / “Really? I …”.
Ss. report one difference with their partner (2–3 Ss.).

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out the role cards (Task F). Ss. role-play the radio interview without looking at the dialogue, then swap roles.
Ss. perform the radio show (2 pairs); the class says which activity each guest loves and which one he / she doesn't care about.
T. gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Reading: The Ciné-Club (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to survey a magazine article to predict its type and content, skim it for the main idea and scan it for specific details about a school film club.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks “Do you watch films at school? Would you like a film club?”
T. pre-teaches screening, projector, sandstorm and membership with the pictures and mime.
T. explains surveying: title, subtitle, headings, source and pictures.
Ss. survey the text for one minute and tick what kind of text it is (Task A); T. writes the predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text in two minutes, reading only the first lines of each paragraph, and tick the main idea (Task B).
T. checks the predictions from Task A: “Which clues helped you?”
T. explains scanning: look only for names, numbers and dates.
Ss. scan the text and answer the detail questions (Task C) against the clock; volunteers write the answers on the board.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task D).
Ss. check in pairs; T. gives feedback with the paragraph headings.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. discuss in pairs: “Would you join the Ciné-Club? Which film would you show?” (Task E)
Ss. write three sentences with their opinion (Task E); 2–3 Ss. read them to the class.
T. announces the next lessons: the club's film, The Last Caravan, will be the model for the film review.

lessons.label: Grammar
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Grammar: Past continuous & simple past (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form the past continuous and use it with the simple past, when and while, to describe actions in progress and interrupted actions in the past.
lessons.point: ① An action in progress at a time in the past: At 4:45, we were watching a film.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “What were you doing yesterday at 8 p.m.?” and accepts any answer.
T. shows the pictures: “Where are they? What happened?”
Ss. read Imane's story and answer: “What happened at 4:45? What was Yassir doing when the power came back?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline was / were + verb-ing in the story and complete the table (Task A); T. checks on the board.
T. highlights spelling: sit → sitting, dance → dancing.
T. draws a timeline for “The guide was crossing the desert when the lights went out.”
T. asks CCQs: “Was the action finished? (no) Which action is short? (went out) Do we use while or when with the short action? (when)”.
Ss. read the Remember box; T. drills weak forms /wəz/, /wə/.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in the past continuous (Task B), then choose the past continuous or the simple past (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models sentence 1 with when.
Ss. join the ideas with when or while (Task D), then read their sentences to a partner.
T. elicits answers and both word orders: “While …, …” / “… when …”.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write a short story about a funny or surprising moment during a leisure activity using while and when (Task E).
Ss. tell their story to a partner, who asks the useful questions; 2–3 Ss. tell the class.
T. notes errors and gives delayed feedback.

lessons.label: Writing - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Writing Part 1: A film review (Process)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to analyse the structure and language of a film review and plan their own review of a film they have watched.
words: The film tells the story of …
The plot is a bit predictable.

stages.name: Pre-writing
steps: T. asks “What was the last film you watched? Would you recommend it?” and recalls the Ciné-Club film The Last Caravan (Reading lesson).
Ss. read Salma's review and answer: “Did Salma like the film? How many stars did she give?”
Ss. number the five parts of the review (Task A); T. checks and labels the parts on the board.
Ss. find the tense, the opinion adjectives, the contrast linker and the recommendation expressions (Task B).
T. elicits: present simple for the plot, no spoilers, a strength and a weakness with However.
Ss. sort the expressions into the four columns (Task C); pair check, then whole-class correction.
Ss. choose a film and brainstorm notes in the grid with the help of the word bank (Task D).
T. monitors and helps with genres and adjectives.
Ss. turn their notes into an outline with the sentence starters (Task E) and write the first sentence of each part.
T. reminds Ss to keep the page for Part 2 (drafting).

lessons.label: Writing - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Writing Part 2: A film review (Process)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write, revise and edit a film review, then produce a final copy using peer feedback.
lessons.point: ① Title + year + stars · ② basic information (genre, director, actors, setting) · ③ plot in the present simple — no ending! · ④ opinion: what you liked + However, a weak point · ⑤ recommendation: I highly recommend it to …

stages.name: Drafting
steps: T. recalls the five parts of a review with the Remember box; Ss. take out their outline from Part 1 (Task E).
Ss. write their first draft (Task A), skipping a line for corrections.
T. monitors and helps with the plot summary in the present simple.

stages.name: Responding / Peer Feedback
steps: Ss. swap drafts and tick the checklist (Task B), then write one compliment and one suggestion.

stages.name: Revising
steps: Ss. read their partner's feedback and improve the content and organisation of their draft: add missing parts, reasons and linkers.

stages.name: Editing
steps: T. presents the correction code (T, P, Sp, WO, C).
Ss. correct the five sentences (Task C); T. checks on the board.
Ss. use the code to check their own draft for tense, prepositions, capitals and spelling.

stages.name: Final Draft
steps: Ss. write the final copy of their review (Task D).
T. collects the reviews; the best ones go on the Ciné-Club page of the school magazine.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Vocabulary: Media words (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words related to the mass media (TV, radio, the press and the Internet) and their word families to talk about their own media habits.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “How did you get the news yesterday?” and writes the answers on the board (TV, radio, phone, newspaper).
Ss. look at the three pictures and say which media they show.
Ss. read Salma's text and answer: “Which media does each person use?” (dad: newspaper · mum: radio · Salma: the Internet · Hamza: TV · grandfather: documentaries).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the six words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and drills the word stress: ˈheadline, ˈchannel, ˈeditor, ˈbroadcast, ˈdocumentary.
Ss. classify the bold words from the text under TV & radio / Newspapers & magazines / Computers & the Internet (Task B).
CCQs: “Does a viewer read or watch?” (watch) “Is a headline long or short?” (short)
T. highlights collocations on the board: switch on the TV, surf the Net, post a comment, change the channel.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the six sentences with the words in the box (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; volunteers read the sentences aloud.
T. corrects on the board and re-drills difficult words (remote control, subscribe).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the word-building table: verb / thing / person (Task D), using a dictionary when needed.
T. elicits the suffixes -er / -or / -ment / -ation.
Ss. complete the sentences with the right form of the word in brackets (Task E).
T. checks and asks Ss to justify the form (noun / verb / plural).

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about how they and their family use the media, with at least six new words (Task F).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who counts the new words.
2–3 Ss. read to the class. T. gives delayed feedback on errors.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Functions: Talking about emotions and feelings (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask about and express emotions, feelings and attitudes when reacting to news, after listening to a radio news bulletin for specific information.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Do you listen to the radio? What kind of news makes you happy or sad?”
Ss. listen to the Radio Our Voice news bulletin and tick the three stories they hear (Task A).
Ss. listen again and complete the notes with specific information: ages, places, days, numbers (Task B). T. checks with the class.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. read and listen to the dialogue and say how Salma and Yassine feel about each story.
Ss. find the underlined expressions and write them in the right column (Task C).
T. builds the board: Asking about feelings / Positive feelings / Negative feelings & attitudes.
CCQs: “Is ‘I'm not really bothered’ positive or negative?” (neither – indifference) “When do we say ‘What a relief!’?” (after a worry ends)
Pronunciation: Ss. classify -ed adjectives by sound /t/ /d/ /ɪd/ (Task D); T. drills them with a wide falling intonation for strong feelings.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the five mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task E).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs act them out.
T. corrects and re-drills intonation.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models headline 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a two-line exchange reacting to each headline, using a different expression each time (Task F).
3–4 pairs perform; the class names the feeling expressed.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out the news cards and role cards A and B (Task G). Ss. role-play: A reads the news, B reacts and explains how he / she feels; they swap roles with a new card.
2–3 pairs perform for the class. T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Reading: Screens, Papers and Teenagers (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to check their predictions, skim a text on teenagers and the mass media for the main ideas and scan it for specific information.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks: “Where did you get the news yesterday?” and tallies the answers on the board.
T. pre-teaches survey, source, reliable, adviser, consume, share with examples.
Ss. look at the title and the three pictures and tick the two ideas they expect in the text (Task A). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. read the text quickly (2 min) to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Were you right? Which words helped you?”
Ss. skim the first lines of each paragraph and match paragraphs 1–4 with their main ideas; one idea is extra (Task B). Pair check.
Ss. scan the text and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task C). Feedback with paragraph numbers.
Ss. scan for numbers to answer the questions (Task D). Volunteers write the answers on the board.
Ss. find what the underlined words refer to (Task E). T. shows how to look back in the sentence before.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. write 3–4 sentences about how they get the news and whether they check it before sharing (Task F).
Ss. compare with a partner; T. collects answers on the board and links to the Writing lesson (an e-mail about media habits).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Grammar Part 1: The passive, present & past simple (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form and use the passive voice in the present simple and past simple to describe how things are made and when they were created.
lessons.point: Active: Mr. Tazi checks the articles. → Passive: The articles are checked (by Mr. Tazi).

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. holds up a newspaper / shows the two pictures and asks: “Who writes a school magazine? Where is it printed?”
Ss. read “How is Our Voice made?” and answer: “Who checks the articles? When was the magazine created?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the underlined verbs and complete the form table: affirmative, form, negative, question (Task A).
T. elicits the rule: be (am / is / are – was / were) + past participle.
T. writes an active sentence and transforms it on the board: Mr. Tazi checks the articles → The articles are checked by Mr. Tazi.
CCQs: “Do the articles check? Who checks?” “Is ‘was printed’ past or present?”
Ss. read the Remember box; T. explains when we use “by + agent”.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the seven sentences with the present or past simple passive (Task B).
Pair check, then feedback; T. focuses on irregular past participles (read, sold, taken).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. rewrite the active sentences in the passive (Task C), using “by” only when the agent is important.
Volunteers write their answers on the board; the class corrects.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: In pairs, Ss. write four quiz questions about the media or famous inventions in the passive (Task D).
Pairs exchange questions with another pair and answer them.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on errors.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Grammar Part 2: The passive, other tenses & modals (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form and use the passive voice with the present continuous, the present perfect, future forms and modals to give news and state rules.
lessons.point: In every passive tense, be changes and the past participle stays: is being made · has been made · will be made · is going to be made · can be made.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. reviews Part 1: “When was our school magazine created? Where is it printed?”
T. shows the pictures of the school radio studio.
Ss. read Yassine's announcement and answer: “When will the first show be broadcast? How can songs be requested?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find an example in the text for each passive form and complete the table (Task A).
T. elicits the pattern: the form of “be” changes, the past participle stays.
CCQs: “The studio is being painted. Is it finished?” (No) “A microphone has been bought. Do we have it now?” (Yes)
T. shows question and negative forms on the board; Ss. read the Remember box.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct passive form in six sentences (Task B).
Pair check, then whole-class feedback.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. rewrite five active sentences in the passive, keeping the same tense or modal (Task C).
Ss. compare; volunteers write their answers on the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write two rules for the media room with modals and two pieces of news about their school with the present perfect or will (Task D).
Ss. read their rules and news to a partner, then to the class. T. gives delayed feedback.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Writing: An e-mail to an e-pal (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write an informal e-mail to an e-pal about their media habits and school news, using e-mail layout, linking words and media vocabulary.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Salma's article (Reading lesson) and asks: “Who is Emily? What did she ask Salma?”
Ss. read Salma's e-mail and answer: “How do her parents get the news? What is her news?”
Ss. number the seven parts of the e-mail (Task A); T. checks and highlights fixed phrases: Thanks for your e-mail. · Write back soon. · Best wishes,

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the right linking word (Task B); T. explains the punctuation with However and so.
Ss. rewrite the e-mail phrases with capital letters, commas, apostrophes and question marks (Task C). Pair check.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. plan their reply to Emily in the outline (Task D): opening, media habits, favourite programme, news, closing — notes only.
Ss. turn their notes into sentences with the sentence starters, then compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their e-mail to Emily (100–120 words) in the e-mail frame (Task E).
Ss. check their e-mail with the checklist and correct it. T. collects the e-mails for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Vocabulary: Celebrations, customs & traditions (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use vocabulary related to celebrations, customs, traditions and occasions to describe how their families celebrate special events.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. writes “Celebrations” on the board and asks: “What occasions do Moroccans celebrate? What do you do on Eid?”
Ss. brainstorm the occasions they know; T. writes them on the board.
T. displays the four pictures; Ss. name the occasions.
Ss. read Imane's text and answer the gist question: “What is Imane's favourite occasion?” (a wedding).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and clarifies meaning with the pictures, examples and CCQs: “Is a guest always a member of the family? (No) Is a feast only food? (No — also a religious celebration)”.
T. drills the pronunciation and word stress of the new words: ceremony, occasion, tradition, relatives, fireworks; Ss. repeat chorally, then individually.
T. writes the words on the board with their stress patterns.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words from the box (Task B).
Ss. put the occasions in the right column (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models one collocation: “We sacrifice a sheep on Eid al-Adha.”
Ss. match the verbs with the nouns (Task D), then write three sentences about their families with three collocations.
Ss. read their sentences to a partner; 2–3 Ss. share them with the class.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write 4–5 sentences about their favourite celebration without naming it (Task E).
Ss. read their descriptions to a partner, who guesses the occasion; 2–3 Ss. read to the class.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Functions: Apologising (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to recognise the topic of short conversations and use formal and informal expressions to apologise and to accept an apology in situations related to celebrations.
lessons.point: Apologise + give a reason: I'm sorry (that) I + past … · I'm sorry for / I apologise for + verb-ing …

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. displays the pictures and asks: “What can go wrong at a party or a wedding? What do you say when you make a mistake?”
T. writes Ss' ideas on the board.
Ss. listen to three short conversations and identify the occasion, the topic and the speaker who apologises (Task A).
T. checks answers.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen again and complete what the speakers say (Task B); T. checks answers.
Ss. put the expressions in the right column (Task C).
T. clarifies with CCQs: “Which is more formal: ‘Sorry about that’ or ‘I apologise for …’? (I apologise for …) What comes after ‘sorry for’? (verb + -ing)”.
T. drills stress and falling intonation (Remember box): I'm SO sorry / NEver mind; Ss. repeat chorally, then individually.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the words from the box (Task D).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs act out the dialogue.
T. corrects on the board and re-drills difficult lines.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a short exchange for each situation (Task E): apology + reason + response, then practise it with a partner.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says which expressions they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task F); Ss. role-play the situation without reading from the worksheet, then swap roles.
2 pairs perform for the class.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Reading: Yennayer (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to survey a text and predict its content, guess the meaning of new words from context and reorder the ideas of a text about a traditional celebration.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks: “When do we celebrate the Amazigh New Year? What do people eat?”
T. displays the pictures; Ss. describe them and guess the topic.
Ss. survey the title, the pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph, then tick three predictions (Task A).
T. writes some predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text to check their predictions, then match each paragraph with its main idea (Task B).
T. ticks or crosses the predictions on the board.
Ss. read again and put the events of the evening in order (Task C); they underline the time markers that helped them.
Ss. guess the meaning of the words from context (Task D).
T. asks: “Which words helped you guess?”
Ss. read carefully and answer the questions (Task E), including one inference question; Ss. compare in pairs.
T. corrects and asks Ss. to justify from the text.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. discuss in pairs: compare Yennayer with another celebration in their region (Task F).
Ss. write 3–4 lines; 2–3 Ss. read their answers to the class.
T. gives feedback and links to the Writing lesson.

lessons.label: Grammar
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Grammar: Relative pronouns & clauses (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the relative pronouns who, which, that, whose, where and when in defining and non-defining relative clauses to describe people, things, places and times related to celebrations.
lessons.point: Defining clause = necessary information, no commas: The guests that came from far away stayed with us. → which guests? that can replace who / which. When the pronoun is the object, we can leave it out: the cake (that) my aunt made.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. displays the pictures and asks: “What's happening? Have you ever been to a henna night?”
Ss. read Imane's blog and answer the gist questions: “Who got married? How long did the wedding last?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the highlighted words and complete the table (Task A).
T. elicits the answers and builds the board: who / which / that / whose / where / when.
T. contrasts two examples: “The guests that came from far away stayed with us.” / “Hamid, who works in Agadir, married Salma.”
CCQs: “Did all the guests stay with us? (No) Do we need the clause to know who Hamid is? (No)”.
T. highlights commas, no “that” and no omission in non-defining clauses (Remember box).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct relative pronoun (Task B).
Ss. decide whether the clauses are defining or non-defining and add commas (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models sentence 1 on the board.
Ss. join the sentences with a relative pronoun (Task D), then compare in pairs.
T. corrects, focusing on the choice of pronoun and on commas.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write definitions of four celebration words with relative clauses, without naming them (Task E).
Ss. read their definitions to a partner, who guesses the words; 2–3 Ss. read theirs to the class.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Writing: A personal letter (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a personal letter to a friend describing a celebration, using the right layout, an informal style and sequencing words.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. asks: “Do you still write letters or long messages to friends? What do you tell them about?”
Ss. read Imane's letter and answer: “What occasion is she writing about? What does she invite Hiba to do?”
Ss. label the parts of the letter (Task A); T. checks and draws the layout on the board.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: T. elicits the features of an informal style: contractions, simple greetings and closings, questions to the reader.
Ss. rewrite the sentences in an informal style (Task B).
Ss. complete Hiba's sentences with the sequencing words and connectors (Task C).
T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. presents the writing task and the outline.
Ss. choose a celebration and plan their letter in the table with the sentence starters (Task D).
Ss. compare their plans in pairs and add details.
T. monitors and helps with vocabulary, the past simple and relative clauses.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their personal letter using their plan (Task E).
Ss. check their letters with the checklist, then swap with a partner for a quick check.
T. collects the letters for marking.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Vocabulary: Arts, crafts & values of Morocco (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use vocabulary related to Morocco's artistic and cultural performances and to Moroccan human values to describe a tradition from their region.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the three pictures (a Gnaoua troupe, a zellige craftsman, mint tea for guests) and asks: “What do these pictures tell us about Morocco?”
Ss. brainstorm the words they know about Moroccan arts, crafts and traditions.
Ss. read Salma's school blog and answer: “What did the students see during Heritage Week? What did Mr. Tazi say about values?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the highlighted words with their meanings (Task A).
T. checks the answers with CCQs: “Is a troupe one person? (No, a group) Does a craftsman use machines? (No, his hands)”.
T. elicits the values words (hospitality, solidarity, respect, generosity, tolerance) and links each one to an example from the text (guests, twiza, elders, Ramadan).
T. models and drills word stress: HERitage, CRAFTSman, hospiTALity, soliDARity.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words from the box (Task B).
Ss. compare their answers; T. corrects on the board and re-drills difficult words.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. presents the suffixes -ity, -ance, -y and -ness with the example hospitable → hospitality.
Ss. complete the word-building table and check the nouns in a dictionary (Task C).
Ss. write a sentence with each noun; volunteers read their sentences aloud.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. models a short description of a tradition from his region with the useful language box.
Ss. write five sentences about an art, a craft or a celebration from their region and the value it shows (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who guesses the value; volunteers share with the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on word choice and pronunciation.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Functions: Expressing possibility (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express possibility (may, might, could, perhaps, it's likely that, there's a good chance that) to talk about the future of Moroccan cultural heritage.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Who is this man? What is zellige? Who is the woman with the microphone?”
Ss. predict what the craftsman may talk about and tick three ideas (Task A).
Ss. listen to the interview for the first time and check their predictions (Task A).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen again for details and take notes in the table (Task B).
T. checks the notes with the class.
Ss. listen again and complete Mr. Benslimane's sentences, then decide if each one shows a stronger or a weaker possibility (Task C).
T. builds the board from the box “Expressing possibility”: may / might / could + infinitive, perhaps / maybe, it's possible / likely that, there's a (good) chance that, I don't think so.
CCQs: “Zellige might disappear — is Driss sure? (No) There's a good chance — more or less sure than might? (more)”.
Pronunciation: might /maɪt/, stress in POSsible and LIKEly, falling intonation; choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue about the Gnaoua Festival with the expressions in the box (Task D).
T. corrects on the board; two volunteers read the dialogue aloud.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models question 1 with a strong student.
Ss. answer the questions, expressing possibility in a different way each time (Task E).
Ss. ask and answer the questions with a partner; 2–3 pairs perform for the class.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task F) and sets the situation: an interview for the school radio “Heritage Voices”.
Ss. prepare their questions and ideas in the notes lines.
Ss. role-play the interview without reading, then swap roles.
Volunteers perform; T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback (*might to …).

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Reading: Al-Qarawiyyin (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to identify the writer's purpose, scan a text for specific information and put its ideas in chronological order.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks: “Which is the oldest university in the world? Where is it?” and accepts the guesses without confirming.
T. pre-teaches key words with pictures and definitions: fortune, scholar, manuscript, restoration, humidity.
Ss. look at the title and the pictures and tick the ideas they expect to find in the text (Task A).

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text in two minutes and check their predictions (Task A).
T. elicits the answers and the words that helped.
Ss. read again, choose the writer's main purpose and copy the persuasive sentence (Task B).
T. elicits the clues: dates, facts and numbers = to inform; “a duty for all of us” = to persuade.
Ss. scan the text and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying from the text (Task C).
T. checks the answers with paragraph references.
Ss. underline the dates and time expressions, then number the events in the order they happened (Task D).
T. corrects on the board as a timeline: inherited fortune → 859 → university → 1981 → 2016.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: T. asks: “Which places in our town are part of our heritage?” and writes the ideas on the board.
Ss. choose a heritage place near them and write 3–4 sentences: what it is, why it is important and how young people can protect it (Task E).
Volunteers read their sentences; the class chooses the place they would most like to visit.
T. links the lesson to the Writing lesson (a biography of a heritage figure).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Grammar Part 1: Conditionals 0 & 1 (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the zero conditional to state facts and the first conditional to talk about real possibilities in the future, in the context of Moroccan crafts and heritage.
lessons.point: Zero conditional: If + present simple, present simple → facts and general truths (if = when): If you heat clay, it becomes hard.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Where are they? What does a potter do?”
T. says: “If you heat ice, it melts. If you work hard, you'll pass.” and asks Ss. what each sentence means.
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “What does Mr. Lahlou offer? Why is it important?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the if-sentences in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
