T. elicits the form: zero = If + present simple, present simple (facts); first = If + present simple, will / won't + infinitive (a real future possibility); comma when the if-clause comes first; no will in the if-clause.
CCQs: “If you heat clay, it becomes hard — true every time? (Yes) If you come every Saturday — is Anas coming for sure? (No)”. T. drills I'll and won't.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in brackets in the correct form, deciding between the zero and the first conditional (Task B).
T. corrects on the board and asks Ss. to explain each choice: a fact or a future possibility?

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with their own ideas (Task C).
Ss. compare their endings with a partner; volunteers read the most original ones to the class.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. models the heritage chain game on the board: “If we clean the old fountain, more visitors will come. If more visitors come, …”
Ss. continue the chain orally, each student starting with the end of the last sentence, then write their best chain (Task D).
Groups read their chains aloud; T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*If it will rain …).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Grammar Part 2: Phrasal verbs (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to understand and use phrasal verbs (grow up, bring up, take after, set up, give up, carry on, pass down, die out, look after, look forward to), with the right object position, to talk about family heritage.
lessons.point: Phrasal verb = verb + particle (up, down, on, after, out …); the meaning is often new: give up ≠ give.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures of a grandmother teaching embroidery and asks: “Who teaches you traditions in your family?”
Ss. read Salma's text and answer: “Who passed the art down to Salma? Will she give it up?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the highlighted phrasal verbs with their meanings (Task A).
T. checks the answers with CCQs: “Many girls gave up embroidery — do they still do it? (No) Grandma carried on — did she stop? (No)”.
T. clarifies the form with the Remember box: verb + particle; separable verbs (pass it down), inseparable verbs (look after it) and verbs with no object (grow up, die out).
T. drills the stress on the particle: grow UP, give UP, die OUT.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the correct form of a phrasal verb from the box (Task B).
T. corrects, focusing on the past forms (grew up, set up) and on -ing after look forward to.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models item 1 on the board: passed down his old oud → passed it down.
Ss. replace the underlined words with a pronoun in the right place (Task C).
Ss. say whether each verb is separable or inseparable; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. interview a partner about his / her family heritage with the questions and note the answers (Task D).
Ss. write a short report, and volunteers present their partner to the class: “Hiba grew up in Taza. She takes after her father …”
T. gives delayed feedback on pronoun position and verb forms.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Writing: A biography (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a one-paragraph biography of a Moroccan heritage figure in chronological order, using the past simple and time expressions.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. shows the pictures and asks: “Do you remember Fatima al-Fihri from the Reading lesson? What did she do?”
Ss. read the model biography and answer: “Where and when was she born? What did she build? Why is she remembered?”
Ss. number the parts of the paragraph in the boxes (Task A).
T. elicits the structure of a paragraph: a topic sentence, supporting sentences in time order and a concluding sentence.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put the sentences of Ben Ali Rbati's biography in the right order and say which words helped them (Task B).
Ss. complete Lalla Fatna's biography with the time expressions from the box (Task C).
T. highlights in + year, on + date and at the age of + age.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. read the fact file about Ibn Battuta; T. checks understanding: “Where was he born? Why did he leave Tangier? How long did he travel?”
Ss. plan their biography by writing notes for each part with the sentence starters (Task D).
T. elicits a topic sentence and a concluding sentence and writes them on the board.
Ss. compare their plans and add any missing information.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write the biography of Ibn Battuta in one paragraph of 100–120 words (Task E).
Ss. revise their paragraph with the checklist and correct their mistakes.
Volunteers read their paragraph aloud; T. collects the paragraphs for feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Vocabulary: Human rights (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use key human rights vocabulary (dignity, equality, discrimination, child labour, illiteracy, freedom of speech …) and build word families with the prefixes un-, in-, il- and dis- to talk about rights in their community.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. writes “10 December — Human Rights Day” on the board and asks: “What is a right? Name one right every child has.”
Ss. brainstorm the rights they know; T. builds a mind map on the board.
T. shows the three pictures and asks: “What problem does each picture show?”
Ss. read the text about the Dignity Club and answer: “Which rights do the students talk about?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the six words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks the answers on the board.
T. clarifies meaning with CCQs: “Is a refugee happy to leave his country? (No) Can an illiterate person read a letter? (No) Is child labour work for adults? (No)”.
T. drills word stress: DIGnity, discrimiNAtion, refuGEE, iLLIteracy, eQUAlity; Ss. repeat chorally, then individually.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; volunteers read the sentences aloud and T. corrects.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. writes equal → unequal → inequality on the board and elicits the opposite prefixes un-, in-, il- and dis-.
Ss. complete the word families (Task C).
Ss. complete the sentences with the correct form of the word in brackets (Task D).
T. checks the answers and highlights il- before l (illegal, illiterate).

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write 4–5 sentences about the three rights that matter most to young Moroccans, using at least four new words (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner and agree on a class “top three”; volunteers present to the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on word use and pronunciation.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Functions: Expressing hopes and wishes (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express hopes (I hope, I'm hoping, Let's hope) and wishes (I wish, If only) about human rights issues, and respond to other people's hopes and wishes in a short interview.
lessons.point: Hope = something possible: I hope / I'm hoping / Let's hope / Hopefully + present simple or will → I hope she comes. I hope it will be a success.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Human Rights Day is coming. What do you hope for our school? What do you wish you could change in the world?” and writes 2–3 answers on the board.
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. listen to the song “One Day” and fill in the gaps (Task A).
Ss. listen again to check and answer: “What does the singer hope for? What does he wish?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find each expression in the song, copy the line and say what comes after it (Task B).
T. elicits the answers and builds the board: hopes (possible) / wishes (unreal now).
CCQs: “I wish the world were fair.” Is the world fair now? (No) Is it real? (No) “I hope he passes.” Is it possible? (Yes)
T. presents the Remember box: I hope + present / will; I wish / If only + past simple, were, could, would; responses (I hope so too. / Let's hope so.)
Pronunciation: weak form of would /wəd/ and the contraction I'd; Ss. repeat chorally.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the dialogue between Salma and Anas with the expressions in the box (Task C).
Ss. check with a partner; two pairs read the dialogue aloud and T. corrects.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a student: “Omar has his driving test tomorrow.” — “I hope he passes!” — “I hope so too.”
Ss. write a hope or a wish for each situation (Task D), then say them to a partner who responds.
3–4 Ss. share their sentences; the class says if each one is a hope or a wish and why.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task E); Ss. prepare short notes.
Ss. role-play the school radio interview, then swap roles.
Two pairs perform for the class; T. notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board (*I wish I will … → I hope I will …).

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Reading: Rights in action (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to identify specific information in a text about four human rights stories and associate pictures with the right paragraphs.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “What is a right? Which rights do some children in villages lose?”
T. pre-teaches wheelchair, ramp, drop out, medina, cooperative and literacy class with pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict which rights the text talks about (Task A — tick three). T. writes the predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text in two minutes to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Were you right? Which words helped you?”
Ss. match each picture with its paragraph and underline the words that helped them (Task B). Feedback with the key words.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task C). Feedback with the paragraph references.
Ss. scan the text for numbers, names and places to answer the questions (Task D); volunteers write the answers on the board.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. write 3–4 sentences about the story that touched them most and what young people could do to help (Task E).
Ss. share their ideas in small groups; each group reports one idea to the class.
T. links Nadia's story to the Writing lesson (a formal letter to ask for help).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Grammar Part 1: Reported speech (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to report statements, questions and requests in reported speech with the correct tense, pronoun and time changes.
lessons.point: Statements: say (that) / tell + person (that) — the tense goes one step back: present simple → past simple · present continuous → past continuous · present perfect / past simple → past perfect · will → would · can → could · must → had to

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. whispers to a student: “I am tired today.” and asks the class: “What did I say to Yassine?” Ss. guess; T. answers: “I said that I was tired that day.”
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. read Imane's report and answer: “What did Mr. Alaoui ask the club to do?” (to write to the council again and not to give up).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the reporting verbs in the report and write Mr. Alaoui's exact words (Task A).
T. checks the answers and builds the direct → reported table on the board.

T. clarifies the rules with the Remember box: say / tell; one tense back (have → had, can → could, will → would); questions with if / wh- + subject + verb; requests with told / asked + (not) to; pronoun and time changes.
CCQs: “Is Mr. Alaoui speaking now? (No) Why couldn't, not can't? (one step back) Can we say ‘He said me’? (No — He told me.)”

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. report what Nadia, Omar, Fatima, Ms. Benali and Hamza said (Task B).
Ss. compare answers; volunteers write them on the board and T. corrects tense and pronoun changes.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. report the questions and the requests in the table (Task C).
T. highlights word order in reported questions (*what did I want → what I wanted) and not to in negative requests.
Quick oral drill: T. says a direct question or order; Ss. report it aloud.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. ask a partner three questions about human rights at school, using the useful questions, and note the answers (Task D).
Ss. write four reported sentences, then report their partner's answers to the class: “I asked Yassine if … . He told me that … .”
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Grammar Part 2: Conditional 2 (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the second conditional (If + past simple, would / could + base verb) to talk about imaginary situations and solutions to human rights problems.
lessons.point: were with all persons: If I were / If she were … · a comma when the if-clause comes first · would → 'd · would not → wouldn't

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Imagine you were the mayor of our town for one day. What would you change?” and writes two answers on the board.
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. read the Dignity Club's ideas wall and say which idea they like most and why.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. answer the questions about the sentences and copy the verbs (Task A).
CCQs: “Is Salma the mayor? (No) Is it real or imaginary? (imaginary) Is it about the past? (No, now)”
Ss. complete the rule; T. clarifies: If + past simple, would / could + base verb; were with all persons; a comma when the if-clause comes first.
T. contrasts conditional 1 (possible) and conditional 2 (imaginary) and drills I'd / wouldn't.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in brackets in the correct form (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board, focusing on question order in sentence 5.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. rewrite each real situation as an imaginary one with If … (Task C), changing positive ↔ negative.
T. checks the answers and links to the Functions lesson: “I wish the school were closer.” → “If the school were closer, Nadia wouldn't miss classes.”

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. pick a card, answer it, then ask their partner the other questions (Task D).
Ss. write their answers and one of their partner's; volunteers report to the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*If I would be … → If I were …).

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Writing: A formal letter (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a formal letter to ask an official for help with a human rights problem, using the layout, formal expressions and linking words of a formal letter.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Nadia's story (Reading lesson) and asks: “Who can help Nadia? How can we ask him or her for help?”
Ss. read Salma's letter and answer: “Who is writing? To whom? Why?”
Ss. number the parts of the formal letter (Task A); T. checks and labels the layout on the board.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. tick the expressions they can use in a formal letter (Task B); T. elicits the features of a formal letter: no contractions, Dear Sir or Madam, Yours faithfully.
Ss. complete the sentences with the linking words (Task C); T. checks and clarifies As a result, However, In addition, because and Therefore.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. reads the situation (Task D) and elicits ideas: the problem, its results and possible requests.
Ss. plan their letter in the outline with the sentence starters (Task D), then turn their notes into sentences.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their formal letter to the Director in the writing frame (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the checklist and correct their mistakes; 1–2 Ss. read their letter aloud.
T. collects the letters for marking with the guide.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Vocabulary: People, Titles & Greetings (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to greet people correctly and talk about the people in their life using vocabulary related to friends, relationships, the social environment, names & titles and greetings.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. greets the class formally and one S informally (“Good morning, everyone!” / “Hi, Salma!”) and asks: “Which greeting is for a friend? Which one is for a teacher?”
T. shows the four pictures; Ss. say who the people are (friends, a teacher, neighbours).
Ss. read Yasmine's text twice and answer: “Who is Sara? Who is Mr. Alami? Who is Mrs. Idrissi?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the words with their meanings (Task A); pair check; T. elicits and confirms.
T. draws a board table of titles: Mr. (man) · Mrs. (married woman) · Miss (woman not married) · Ms. (any woman) + family name. CCQ: “Can we say ‘Mr. Ali’? (No — Mr. + family name: Mr. Bennani)”.
T. sorts greetings: formal (Good morning / afternoon / evening) · informal (Hi, Hello) · leaving (Bye, See you, Good night).
Pronunciation: neighbour /ˈneɪbə/, colleague /ˈkɒliːɡ/, Mrs. /ˈmɪsɪz/ — choral & individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B); pair check; T. corrects.
Ss. cross out the odd word in each line (Task C) and justify orally: “Hello — it isn't a title.”

stages.name: Internalize
steps: In pairs, Ss. join each word with its partner (shake hands, make friends, best friend, say hello, next-door neighbour) and write one sentence for each (Task D).
T. elicits sentences; volunteers act out “shake hands / say hello”.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Mingle: each S gets a role card (teacher Mr./Mrs. …, neighbour, best friend, new classmate) and greets 4 classmates with the right greeting and title; they say goodbye appropriately.
Ss. write three sentences about people in their life (Production) and read them to a partner, who checks the title and the greeting.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Functions: Introductions (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use expressions to introduce themselves, introduce someone and exchange personal information (name, age, city, phone number) when they meet new classmates.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. enters and greets the class: “Hello! I'm Mr. Nejjar. What's your name?” and shakes hands with 2–3 Ss.
T. elicits Ss' answers: “Hello! I'm …”.
T. displays the two pictures and asks: “Where are they? Do they know each other?”
Ss. listen to / read the dialogue and answer the gist question: “Who is new at school?” (Adam).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the expressions in the dialogue and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. elicits answers and builds the board: Introducing oneself / Introducing someone / Exchanging personal information.
CCQs: “Do Hiba and Adam know each other before? (No) When do we say ‘Nice to meet you’? (the first time we meet someone) ‘This is Karim’ — is it about me or another person? (another person)”.
Form & pronunciation: I'm / name's / what's / he's (contractions); falling intonation in Wh- questions; choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs read the dialogue aloud.
T. corrects on the board and re-drills difficult lines.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models cue 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write and practise a short exchange for each situation (Task C), then swap roles.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says which expression they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task D). Ss. role-play meeting a new student without looking at the dialogue.
Pairs join another pair; each S introduces his / her partner: “This is … . He's / She's … .”
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Reading: A New Pen Friend (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to show understanding of the text “Hello from Morocco!” by identifying specific details about the writer and her friends.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “Do you have a friend in another city or country? How do you talk to him / her?”
T. pre-teaches pen friend, kind, funny, strict with pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the letter to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Was your prediction right? Which words helped you?”
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task B). Pair check; feedback with the lines.
Ss. scan the text to answer the detail questions (Task C); volunteers write the answers on the board.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. answer Nour's three questions about themselves (Task D).
Ss. read their answers to a partner; 2–3 Ss. read to the class.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Grammar: the verb be (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to talk about themselves and their classmates (name, age, origin, class) using the verb be in the present simple — affirmative, negative and interrogative forms — in a “Two truths and a lie” game.
lessons.point: I → am · he / she / it → is · you / we / they → are · Question: be first → Are you new?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. points and says: “I'm your teacher. You are students. Is Yassine here today? — Yes, he is.” and asks 2–3 Ss similar questions.
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Is Hicham new? Are Amine and Hamza brothers? Is the library open?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline every form of be in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A) in pairs.

T. elicits the table and clarifies the form: I + am · he / she / it + is · you / we / they + are; contractions ('m, 's, 're); negative with not (isn't, aren't, but I'm not); questions by inversion (Are you …?); short answers without contraction (Yes, I am).
CCQs: “Ali and Omar — is or are? Can we say ‘Yes, I'm’? (No)”. Drill contractions and rising intonation in Yes / No questions.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with am, is or are — affirmative (✓) or negative (✗) (Task B).
Pair check; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. make each sentence negative, then write the Yes / No question and a short answer (Task C).
Ss. ask and answer the questions in pairs, changing the names to classmates' names.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Two truths and a lie”: Ss. write three sentences about themselves — two true, one false (Task D).
Partners ask Yes / No questions (“Are you from …? Is your best friend …?”) to find the lie.
Volunteers report to the class: “Salma isn't from Fez. She's from Meknes.”
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*He from …, *Yes, I'm).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Grammar: plural nouns (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to describe their class and their neighbourhood using regular and irregular plural nouns in an “Our class in numbers” survey.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. points: “One boy … two boys. One girl … three girls. One teacher … how many teachers do you have?”
Ss. read Rania's text “My building” and answer: “How many families are there? What pets are there?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the plural of each noun in the text and complete the rule table with one more example (Task A).
T. elicits the rules: +s · +es after s, ss, sh, ch, x, o · consonant + y → ies but vowel + y → s · f / fe → ves · irregular (men, women, children, people, feet, teeth, mice).
CCQs: “Baby → babies; boy → boys. Why different? (vowel before y)”. Pronunciation: /s/ books · /z/ friends · /ɪz/ classes — Ss. sort the words in the sound box.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. write the plural of twelve nouns (Task B); race in pairs, then check with the rule table.
T. corrects; quick-fire oral drill (T. says the singular, Ss. say the plural).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. rewrite the sentences in the plural, changing the noun and the verb be (Task C) — “My friend is from Fez.” → “My friends are from Fez.”
Pair check; volunteers write answers on the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Our class in numbers”: in groups of 4, Ss. count and write four sentences about the class and their street (Task D): “There are 16 boys and 14 girls. There are two women in my family.”
Each group reads its sentences; other groups check the numbers and the plurals.
T. gives delayed feedback (*childs, *peoples, *familys).

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 1 — Writing: A letter to a pen friend (Product)
lessons.topic: A letter to a pen friend
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to produce an informal letter to a new pen friend about themselves and their friends, using the verb be, personal-information vocabulary and the layout of a letter.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Nour's letter (Reading lesson): “Who is Emma? What does Nour ask her?”
Ss. read Emma's reply and answer: “How old is Emma? Who is her best friend?”
Ss. label the seven parts of the letter (Task A); T. checks and highlights the fixed phrases: Dear …, · Thank you for your letter. · Please write back soon. · Best wishes, + name.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put the parts of Sami's letter in the right order (Task B); pair check.
Ss. rewrite the lines with capital letters, commas, apostrophes and question marks (Task C).

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. plan their letter to Emma in the outline (Task D): about me · my school · my friends · my questions — notes only.
Ss. turn the notes into sentences with the sentence starters (I'm … / My best friend is … . She's …), then compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write the full letter (60–80 words) in the letter frame (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the self-assessment checklist and correct it. T. collects the letters for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Vocabulary: School life (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words about school rules, timetables and school activities, and common collocations (do homework, take notes, pass an exam, join a club, make mistakes) to talk about their school life.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures (a timetable, students in uniform, the basketball team) and asks: “Where are these students? What do you see on a school timetable?”
Ss. guess and give words they know.
Ss. read Salma's text twice and answer the gist question: “What does Salma do after school?” (reading club, basketball team, homework).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: T. clarifies the highlighted words with the pictures, mime and examples; Ss. match each word with its meaning (Task A).
T. checks the answers and asks CCQs: “Can you use your phone in class? (No, it's forbidden.) Is the break a lesson? (No.)”
T. presents collocations: do homework, take notes, pass an exam, join a club, make mistakes.
Ss. put the words in the right column (Task C).
T. drills stress: TIMEtable, SUBject, UNIform, forBIDden, reVISE.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
Ss. complete the sentences with do, take, pass, join or make (Task D).
T. corrects on the board; Ss. read the sentences aloud.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models one answer: “My favourite subject is English.”
Ss. answer the questions about their own school with the new words (Task E).
Ss. ask and answer the questions with a partner; T. invites a few Ss. to share.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about their school life: timetable, two rules, an activity and two collocations (Task F).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who checks the collocations.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Functions: Interest & preference (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express interest (That's a good idea! / That sounds interesting!) and preference (I prefer … / I'd rather … / I like … better than …) when talking about school activities, and pronounce /θ/ and /ð/ correctly.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “What clubs are there in our school? Which club do you like?”
T. sets the context: Salma and Mehdi choose a school club on Clubs' Day.
Ss. read the short dialogue silently once and complete the table with the day, time and place of each club (Task A).
Ss. say which club Salma and Mehdi choose (the environment club).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. read it again and tick the expressions they find (Task B).
Ss. put the expressions in the right column: interest or preference, then add one more to each (Task C).
T. clarifies form and use: I prefer + noun, I'd rather + verb, I like A better than B; CCQs: “Is ‘I'd rather work outside’ Salma's first choice? (Yes)”.
Ss. repeat words with /θ/ and /ð/ after T. and classify them (Task D); T. drills the expressions with natural intonation.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogues with the correct expression (Task E).
T. checks the answers; Ss. read the mini-dialogues aloud with a partner.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models item 1 with a student: “Let's join the school choir!” — “That sounds great!”
Ss. answer each suggestion, showing interest or saying what they prefer (Task F), then practise the exchanges orally.
T. invites a few Ss. to perform.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. use role cards A and B to plan their Clubs' Day: suggest activities, show interest, express preferences and decide together (Task G).
Ss. tell the class their choice: “We'd rather organise a reading competition because …”
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Reading: A letter from Meknes (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to scan a letter about school life to find specific information (numbers, names, days, times and places) quickly and accurately.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “How many students are there in our school? What time does our school day start? What's your favourite subject?”
T. pre-teaches cousin, strict, member and plant trees with the pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the pictures and the layout of the text, then tick who writes it and to whom (Task A).
T. collects the predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. check their prediction quickly (Task A): a letter from Salma to her cousin Yassine.
T. presents the “How to scan” steps: decide what you need (number, name, day, time, place), move your eyes quickly, stop and read the sentence.
Scanning race: Ss. find the answers to the five questions in two minutes and underline them in the text (Task B).
Ss. compare their answers; T. checks them on the board and asks “Which word helped you find it?”
Ss. decide if the statements are true or false and justify with words from the text (Task C).
T. gives feedback with the line references.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. answer Salma's questions about their favourite subject and school activities (Task D).
Ss. read their answers to a partner; 2–3 Ss. read to the class.
T. tells Ss. that their answers will help them write a letter about school life in the Writing lesson.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Grammar Part 1: the present simple (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the present simple in the affirmative, negative and interrogative forms to talk about school routines and habits.
lessons.point: he / she / it → verb + -s: walks, plays · -es after o, ch, sh, ss, x: goes, watches · consonant + y → -ies: study → studies · have → has

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “What time do you get up? How do you come to school?” and writes two answers on the board.
Ss. look at the pictures, read the dialogue and answer: “How does Anas go to school? What does Mehdi do after school?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the verbs in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
T. checks the answers and builds the board: affirmative, negative, question, short answers.
T. clarifies with the Remember box: he / she / it + -s, -es, -ies, has; don't / doesn't + base verb; Do / Does + subject + base verb.
CCQs: “She studies at university — a habit or now? (a habit)”. T. drills the -s endings /s/, /z/, /ɪz/.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in brackets in the present simple (Task B).
Ss. check their answers with a partner; T. corrects on the board and focuses on -s and doesn't + base verb.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models prompt 1: “Do you get up at 6:30?” — “No, I don't. I get up at 7.”
Ss. write the questions, ask their partner and note the answers (Task C).
A few Ss. report: “Hamza doesn't get up at 6:30. He gets up at 7.”

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. interview a classmate about his / her school day with the useful questions (Task D).
Ss. write five sentences about their classmate for the school magazine; 2–3 Ss. read them to the class.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on -s, don't / doesn't and question order.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Grammar Part 2: prepositions of time (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to correctly talk about school timetables, dates and activities using the prepositions of time in, on, at and from …
words: the start and the end of a period
lessons.point: in the morning / afternoon / evening — BUT at night · on Monday morning (day + part of the day) · at the weekend

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “When do we have English? What time does school start? When are the exams?” and writes the answers on the board.
Ss. look at the pictures and read the school notice to answer: “When are the final exams? When is the library closed?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the highlighted prepositions, complete the rule with the words in the box and add examples from the notice (Task A).
T. clarifies with a timeline: at + clock time → on + day / date → in + month / year; from … to for a period.
CCQs: “on 21st March — a month or a date? (a date)”. T. highlights the Remember box: in the morning BUT at night; on Monday morning.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct preposition (Task B).
Ss. compare answers; T. corrects on the board and asks Ss. to justify each answer with the rule.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models: “When is your birthday?” — “It's on 12th April.”
Ss. answer the questions about themselves in full sentences (Task C), then ask and answer them with a partner.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. create a new school club and write a notice with the day, the time (from … to), the place and a special event (Task D).
Ss. present their notices to the class; the class chooses the club they want to join.
T. gives delayed feedback on the prepositions.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 2 — Writing: A letter about school life (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a letter of 60–80 words to a friend about their school life (school, timetable, subjects, rules and activities) with the correct layout and the linking words and, but and because.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss. of Salma's letter from the Reading lesson and asks: “Who writes? To whom? Why?”
Ss. read the model letter and number its parts (Task A).
T. checks and writes the layout of a letter on the board: greeting, opening, body, questions, closing, name.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put Yassine's reply in the right order (Task B).
T. clarifies and / but / because with examples from the model (… English because our teacher …).
Ss. join the sentences with and, but or because (Task C); T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. brainstorms ideas with the class: school name, city, timetable, favourite subject, rules, activities.
Ss. plan their reply to Salma and write notes with the sentence starters (Task D).
T. models how to turn notes into sentences on the board.
Ss. turn two of their notes into full sentences and check them with a partner.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their letter to Salma about their school life, 60–80 words (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the checklist and correct it.
T. collects the letters; 2 Ss. read their letters to the class.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Vocabulary: Household articles, clothes & shopping (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words for household articles, clothes and shopping to talk and write about what their family needs to buy.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows a shopping bag and takes out real things or pictures (a plate, a scarf, a receipt) and asks: “Where do we buy these? Do you like shopping?”
Ss. name the things they know.
T. displays the three pictures (Context) and asks: “Where are the people? What can you buy there?”
Ss. read Hind's text and answer the gist question: “What does Hind's family buy?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match each highlighted word with its meaning (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks and builds the board in three groups: Household articles / Clothes / Shopping.
T. clarifies meaning with pictures, mime (try on) and CCQs: “Is a receipt money? (No) Is a shop assistant a customer? (No) Are things on sale cheap or expensive? (cheaper)”.
Pronunciation: silent “p” in receipt, trousers /ˈtraʊzəz/, stress in exPENsive and asSIStant; choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
Pair check; T. corrects on the board and Ss. read the sentences aloud.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. find the odd word in each line and say why (Task C): “Scarf, because it's clothes, not a kitchen article.”
Ss. put the words in the right column and add two words of their own to each column (Task D).
Groups compare lists; T. adds new words to the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. imagine their family is moving to a new flat: they write a shopping list and sentences with the new words (Production): “We need a … for the kitchen. I want new … because …”.
Ss. read their list to a partner, who asks: “Why do you need it? Is it expensive?”
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on spelling and pronunciation.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Functions Part 1: Asking for & giving opinions (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask for and give opinions about clothes and things in a shop (What do you think of …? / I think … / In my opinion, …) in a shopping role-play.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows a picture of a jacket and asks two Ss: “Do you like this jacket? Is it nice?”
Ss. answer freely; T. writes one answer on the board: “I think it's nice.”
T. displays the two pictures and asks: “Where are the girls? What are they doing?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer the gist question: “What does Kawtar want to buy? Why?” (a dress for her cousin's wedding).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the expressions in the dialogue and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. elicits answers and builds the board: Asking for an opinion / Positive opinion / Negative opinion.
CCQs: “‘How do you like them?’ — is Kawtar asking for a price or an opinion? (an opinion) Why ‘them’? (the shoes — plural) Is ‘I don't like it very much’ positive or negative? (negative)”.
Form: What do you think of + it / them? · I think + sentence · In my opinion, + sentence; choral then individual drilling of the exponents.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task B).
Pair check, then open pairs read the dialogue aloud; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models cue 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a short exchange for each situation (Task C), then practise it with a partner and swap roles.
2–3 pairs perform; the class says if the opinion is positive or negative.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task D). Ss. role-play shopping for Eid clothes without looking at the dialogue: A asks for opinions, B gives opinions with reasons.
Two pairs perform for the class; the class says what A decides to buy.
T. gives delayed feedback on errors noted while monitoring.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Functions Part 2: Asking about prices (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask about and give prices (How much is / are …? — It's / They're … dirhams) and bargain politely when buying and selling at a shop or souk.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. holds up a pen and a pair of socks with price tags and asks: “Is this pen expensive? Guess the price!”
Ss. guess; T. answers: “It's 5 dirhams. They're 20 dirhams.”
T. displays the two pictures and asks: “Where is Ayoub? Who is the man?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer the gist questions: “What does Ayoub buy? How much does he pay?” (a T-shirt and jeans, 300 dirhams).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the expressions in the dialogue and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. elicits answers and builds the board: Asking about prices / Giving prices / Reacting and bargaining.
CCQs: “Why ‘How much is’ for the T-shirt but ‘How much are’ for the jeans? (one thing / plural) Does ‘a discount’ make the price higher or lower? (lower) Who says ‘Here's your change’? (the seller)”.
Form: How much is + singular? → It's … · How much are + plural? → They're …; numbers (15 / 50, 90 / 19); choral then individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task B).
Pair check, then open pairs read the dialogue aloud; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models cue 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a short exchange for each price tag (Task C), then practise it with a partner and swap roles.
2–3 pairs perform; the class checks is / are and the numbers.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task D). Ss. role-play buying and selling at the souk: the customer buys three things with 600 DH, bargains and counts the change.
Ss. change roles with a new partner; one pair performs for the class, who say what the customer bought and how much change he / she got.
T. gives delayed feedback on errors noted while monitoring.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Reading: Hind's shopping habits (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to identify explicit details (who, when, where, why, how much) in a letter about shopping habits and talk about their own shopping habits.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “Where do you buy your clothes? Do you like shopping? Who do you go shopping with?”
T. pre-teaches souk, shopping mall, bargain, pocket money and save with the pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the letter to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Was your prediction right? Which words helped you?”
T. explains the strategy: explicit details are written in the text, so we find the exact words and underline them.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task B). Pair check; feedback with the lines.
Ss. scan the text for the details to answer the questions (Task C): who, when, why, how much, where.
Volunteers write the answers on the board and show the line in the text.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. answer Hind's three questions about their own shopping habits (Task D).
Ss. read their answers to a partner, who finds one difference: “You prefer the souk, but I prefer the mall.” 2–3 Ss. report to the class.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Grammar Part 1: Comparatives (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to compare shops, places and products using comparative adjectives (short adjectives + -er, more + long adjectives, better / worse) + than.
lessons.point: short adjective + -er + than: The souk is cheaper than the mall. · long adjective: more + adjective + than: more expensive than

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows two price tags (a pen 5 DH, a pen 15 DH) and asks: “Which pen is cheap? Which is expensive?” T. says: “This pen is cheaper than that pen.”
T. displays the two pictures (the souk / the mall).
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Where do Hind and Ayoub go in the end? Why?” (the mall — it's raining).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the comparatives in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A) in pairs.

T. elicits the table and clarifies the form: short adjective + -er + than; spelling (big → bigger, close → closer, friendly → friendlier); long adjective: more + adjective + than; irregular good → better, bad → worse.
CCQs: “The souk is cheaper than the mall — which one is more expensive? Can we say ‘more cheaper’? (No)”. Drill the sentences with weak “than” /ðən/.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. write the comparative form of the adjectives in brackets (Task B).
Pair check; T. corrects on the board, focusing on spelling.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. compare the two things in each line using the information and the adjective, then write a second sentence with the opposite adjective (Task C).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who checks -er / more and than.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Which is better?”: Ss. choose two places or things (the souk / the mall, online / in a shop …) and write four comparative sentences (Task D).
Ss. discuss their choice with a partner: “I think the souk is better because it's cheaper.” Volunteers report to the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*more cheaper, *than / that).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Grammar Part 2: Pronouns & possessives (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use subject and object pronouns, possessive adjectives and possessive pronouns correctly to say who things belong to (Whose … is this? — It's mine / hers).
lessons.point: Subject pronoun before the verb: She buys … · Object pronoun after a verb or preposition: Give them to me.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. takes a student's pen and asks: “Whose pen is this? Is it yours?” — S: “Yes, it's mine.” T. repeats with 2–3 objects and writes one exchange on the board.
T. displays the two pictures and asks: “Where are they? What's in the bags?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Whose scarf is it? Whose trainers are they?” (Kawtar's · Ayoub's).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the highlighted words in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A) in pairs.

T. elicits the table and clarifies: subject pronoun before the verb; object pronoun after a verb or a preposition; possessive adjective + noun (my jacket); possessive pronoun alone (It's mine); its ≠ it's; Whose …? → It's Kawtar's / hers.
CCQs: “‘It's mine.’ — is there a noun after mine? (No) Can we say ‘mine jacket’? (No)”. Drill Whose …? — It's mine / yours / his / hers.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct word in each sentence (Task B).
Pair check; T. corrects on the board and asks Ss. to say why (before / after the verb, + noun or alone).

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. rewrite the sentences, replacing the underlined words with a pronoun or a possessive (Task C).
Ss. compare with a partner; volunteers write their sentences on the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Whose is it?” game: in groups of four, Ss. put one personal thing each in a box, take one and ask: “Whose … is this? Is it yours?” — “No, it isn't mine. I think it's hers.” (Task D)
Ss. write four sentences about the things in their group (Task D); volunteers read them to the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*mine jacket, *to she, *it's / its).

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 3 — Writing: A reply letter (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write an informal reply letter to a pen friend about their shopping habits, giving opinions and using comparatives, possessives and the layout of a letter.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Hind's letter (Reading lesson): “Who is Hind? What three questions does she ask?”
Ss. read Yasmine's reply and answer: “Does Yasmine prefer the souk or the mall? Why?”
Ss. label the eight parts of the reply letter (Task A); T. checks and highlights the fixed phrases: Dear …, · Thank you for your letter. · Please write back soon. · Best wishes, + name.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put the parts of Othmane's reply in the right order (Task B); pair check.
Ss. rewrite the lines with capital letters, commas, full stops, apostrophes and question marks (Task C); T. corrects on the board (its / it's, brother's).

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. plan their reply to Hind in the outline (Task D): opening · where I shop · my opinion · pocket money · my questions — notes only.
Ss. turn the notes into sentences with the sentence starters (I prefer … because it's cheaper than … / In my opinion, …), then compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write the full reply letter (60–80 words) in the letter frame (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the self-assessment checklist and correct it. T. collects the letters for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Vocabulary: Cinema, theatre, music & art (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words about cinema, theatre, music and art, and common arts collocations, to talk and write about their artistic interests.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the four pictures and asks: “What can you see? Which one do you like most: cinema, theatre, music or art?”
Ss. name the places / activities they know.
Ss. read Hajar's blog and answer the gist question: “Which arts does Hajar love?” (cinema, theatre, art and music).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the highlighted words and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. elicits answers and builds a word map on the board: Cinema / Theatre / Music / Art.
T. checks meaning with pictures, mime and CCQs: “Is a stage in a cinema or a theatre?” “Does a painter sing?”
T. drills pronunciation and stress: theatre, exhibition, gallery, concert, audience.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. find the ten arts words in the word search and write C, T, M or A next to each one (Task B).
Ss. match the verbs with the words to make collocations (Task C).
T. corrects on the board: watch a film, play the guitar, visit an exhibition…

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the collocations in the box (Task D).
Ss. check in pairs; T. elicits answers and Ss. read the sentences aloud.
T. asks quick personal questions with the collocations: “When do you watch a film?” “Do you play the guitar?”
Ss. answer with full sentences.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four sentences about their artistic interests, using four words and two collocations from the lesson (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who finds one thing they have in common.
T. invites 3–4 Ss. to share and gives feedback on word use and spelling.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Functions Part 1: Likes & dislikes (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to express likes and dislikes about films, music, theatre and art, and pronounce the third-person -s correctly.
lessons.point: I love / like / enjoy / don't mind / hate / can't bear + noun or verb-ing: I love music. I enjoy playing the guitar.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. tells the class: “I love films, but I can't bear horror films!” and asks: “What about you?”
Ss. answer freely.
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “What does Kenza love? What does Anas hate?” (painting / horror films).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the highlighted expressions and write them in the right column (Task A).
T. builds a scale on the board: ☺☺ love / adore … ☹☹ hate / can't bear.
T. clarifies form: love / enjoy / don't mind + noun or verb-ing (Remember box).
Pronunciation: Ss. say the verbs and classify the -s ending as /s/, /z/ or /ɪz/ (Task B); T. drills watches, dances, practises.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs read the mini-dialogues aloud.
T. corrects and re-drills difficult lines.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models cue 1: “Yasmine loves dancing.”
Ss. write a sentence for each cue, using a different expression each time (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences; T. checks the -s ending and verb-ing.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task E). Ss. role-play the Arts Club survey and give reasons, then swap roles.
Ss. report to the class about their partner: “Kenza loves painting, but she can't bear …”
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Functions Part 2: Inviting (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to invite friends to artistic events and accept or refuse invitations politely, giving a reason.
lessons.point: Would you like to / Do you want to + verb: Would you like to come? · How about + verb-ing: How about inviting Yasmine?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the film night poster and asks: “What is it? When is it? Would you like to go?”
Ss. answer freely.
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Where are Mehdi and Salma going? When?” (to film night, Saturday at six).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the highlighted expressions and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. builds the board: Inviting / Accepting / Refusing.
T. clarifies form: Would you like to + verb; How about + verb-ing (Remember box).
CCQs: “Does Salma go for a juice? (No) Is she polite? (Yes — she says sorry and gives a reason.)”
T. drills the expressions with rising intonation on the invitations.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs and read the dialogue aloud; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models invitation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. accept or refuse each invitation as in the cue, giving a reason when they refuse (Task C).
Pairs read their exchanges; the class checks that each refusal has a reason.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task D). Ss. role-play inviting and answering with their diaries, then swap roles.
Ss. write their weekend plan; 2–3 pairs perform for the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Reading: Meet Nada, the young artist (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to scan the text “Meet Nada, the young artist of Ouarzazate” to find factual details such as ages, numbers, places and days.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “Do you know a young artist? What does he / she do?”
T. pre-teaches kasbah, exhibition, fine arts, film studio and oud with the pictures.
Ss. look at the title and the pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option).
T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. skim the text to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Which words helped you?”
Ss. decide if the statements are true or false and justify with words from the text (Task B).
Pair check; feedback with the lines.
T. shows how to scan: read the fact, find the key word (a number, a day, a place), then read that sentence.
Ss. complete Nada's fact file (Task C); volunteers write the answers on the board.
Ss. answer the detail questions (Task D); T. checks orally.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. write three sentences about which of Nada's activities they would like to do and why (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner; 2–3 Ss. read to the class.
T. gives feedback and links to the next lesson (Nada's week).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Grammar Part 1: Adverbs of frequency (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use adverbs of frequency in the right position to talk about their artistic habits.
lessons.point: Adverb before the main verb: I often listen to music. · She usually paints at the weekend.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “How often do you go to the cinema?” and writes Ss' answers on the board.
Ss. look at the pictures and read Nada's week; they answer: “How often does Nada paint?” (usually, at the weekend).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the highlighted adverbs and put them on the scale from 100% to 0% (Task A).
T. checks meaning with CCQs: “I rarely watch TV — a lot? (No, almost never)”.
Ss. complete the two sentences about position (Task A); T. builds the rule: adverb before the main verb, after be (Remember box).
T. drills pronunciation: always, usually, often.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the adverb in the right place and rewrite the sentences (Task B).
Pair check; volunteers write the sentences on the board; T. corrects.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models sentence 1 from Othmane's week: “He always practises the guitar.”
Ss. write a sentence for each activity with the right adverb (Task C).
T. checks the position after be (He is usually tired) and the -s ending.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. ask a partner “How often do you …?” and complete the arts habits survey (Task D).
Ss. write three sentences comparing themselves with their partner; 3–4 Ss. read them aloud.
T. gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Grammar Part 2: How often / long / many / much (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask and answer questions with How often, How long, How many and How much about artistic hobbies.
lessons.point: How many + plural noun: How many paintings …? · How much + uncountable noun: How much time / money …?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures and asks: “Who is he? What does he play?”
Ss. read the interview and answer: “What instrument does Othmane play? How many people are in his band?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match each question word with what it asks about and find an example answer in the interview (Task A).
T. clarifies form: question word + do / does + subject + verb; How many + plural noun; How much + uncountable noun / price (Remember box).
CCQs: “Can we count guitars? Can we count music?”; T. drills the questions.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the questions with How often, How long, How many or How much (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs, then read the questions and answers aloud in open pairs.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models item 1: “How often does Nada paint?”
Ss. write questions for the underlined words (Task C).
Volunteers write the questions on the board; T. corrects do / does and the noun after many / much.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write one question with each question word about a classmate's favourite art or hobby (Task D).
Ss. interview a classmate and note the answers.
Ss. write a short report and tell the class about their classmate.
T. gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 4 — Writing: A film review (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a short film review with basic information, the story, their opinion and a rating.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. shows the film poster and asks: “What kind of film is it? Do you read film reviews?”
Ss. read Kenza's review and answer: “Does Kenza like the film?” (Yes, but not the ending.)
Ss. number the parts of the review in the boxes (Task A).
T. writes the layout on the board: title – basic information – story – opinion – rating.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. match the adjectives with their meanings (Task B); T. checks and drills them.
Ss. complete the sentences with and, but, because or so (Task C).
T. corrects on the board and points out the linkers in Kenza's review.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. elicits films Ss. know and brainstorms types of films on the board (comedy, cartoon, drama, action).
Ss. choose a film and write notes for each part using the sentence starters (Task D).
T. goes round and helps with vocabulary.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their film review (60–80 words) for the school magazine (Task E).
Ss. check their review with the checklist and correct their mistakes.
T. collects the reviews for marking.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Vocabulary: Food, meals & eating habits (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words about food, meals, preparing meals and eating habits to describe their own family's eating habits.
lessons.point: have breakfast / lunch / dinner · skip a meal · plan the meals · prepare a meal · make a shopping list · a healthy snack / diet · wash, peel, chop, boil, fry vegetables

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the three pictures and asks: “What can you see? What do you usually have for breakfast?”
Ss. answer and T. writes their food words on the board.
Ss. read Salma's text and answer the gist question: “Which meal does Salma never skip?” (breakfast).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks the answers and shows meaning with pictures and mime (wash, peel, chop).
T. asks CCQs: “Is an apple at 10 a.m. a meal or a snack? (a snack) If I skip lunch, do I eat at 1 p.m.? (No)”
T. models and drills vegetables, breakfast, dessert (≠ desert); Ss. repeat chorally, then individually.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; volunteers read the sentences aloud and T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. put the words from the box in the right group: Meals, Food, Preparing food, Eating habits (Task C).
Ss. add one word of their own to each group.
T. elicits the new words, reads the collocations in the Remember box with the class and adds them to the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about their family's eating habits with the new words (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner and find two differences; 2–3 Ss. report to the class.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on word use.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Functions (Part 1): Agreeing & disagreeing (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to agree and disagree with other people's opinions about food and eating habits, giving a simple reason.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. says: “I love pizza!” and asks 3–4 Ss.: “Do you like pizza too?” T. writes their answers on the board.
T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Where are they? What are they talking about?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Who likes pizza? Who prefers couscous?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the expressions in the dialogue and write them in the right column (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. builds the board: Agreeing / Disagreeing.
T. asks CCQs: “Hamza says ‘I don't like vegetables.’ Nora agrees: So do I or Me neither? (Me neither) Is ‘Surely not!’ soft or strong? (strong)”
T. models stress and intonation: Me TOO! · SUREly NOT!; Ss. repeat chorally, then individually.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; open pairs read the exchanges aloud with the right intonation.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models statement 1 with a strong student.
Ss. agree or disagree with each statement and write a reason (Task C), then read their answers to a partner.
3–4 Ss. read a statement aloud; the class reacts with an agreeing or disagreeing expression and a reason.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task D). Ss. role-play the food debate, giving opinions and reacting to each one with a reason.
Pairs note three things they agree on and report to the class.
T. monitors, notes errors (Me too / Me neither) and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Functions - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Functions (Part 2): Ordering a meal (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to order a meal politely in a restaurant and ask for the bill, and take a customer's order as a waiter.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Do you go to restaurants? What do you order?” and writes Ss' food words on the board.
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “What do Salma and her father order?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. decide who says each expression and write it in the right column (Task A).
T. checks and builds the board: The waiter says / The customer says.
T. asks CCQs: “Who asks ‘Anything else?’ (the waiter) Is ‘I want the fish’ polite? (not very) What is ‘the bill’? (the paper with the price)”
T. drills I'd like / Can I have …, please? with polite rising intonation.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the waiter–customer dialogue with the words in the box (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs, then open pairs perform it.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1.
Ss. write what they say in each situation (Task C), then practise the exchanges with a partner and swap roles.
3 pairs act out one situation; the class says which expression they used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. sets up a restaurant corner. Ss. role-play the waiter and the customer with the Dar Salam menu and the role cards (Task D): order a full meal, then ask for the bill.
Ss. swap roles and write their order and the bill.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on polite forms and prices.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Reading: What do Fez teenagers eat? (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to scan the text “What do Fez teenagers eat?” to find specific numbers and details quickly, and read and recite a short poem about healthy food.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks: “What do you have for breakfast? How often do you eat fast food?”
T. pre-teaches survey, results, fizzy drinks and worried with pictures and examples.
Ss. look at the title and the four pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A — tick one option). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. read the text quickly to check their predictions (Task A). T. asks: “Was your prediction right? Which words helped you?”
T. explains scanning: look only for the numbers, don't read every word.
Ss. scan the text in two minutes and write what each number refers to (Task B). Pair check; feedback with the paragraph.
Ss. scan the text to decide if the statements are true or false and justify with words from the text (Task C). Volunteers read the justifications aloud.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: T. reads the poem aloud; Ss. underline the food words. Ss. read it chorally, then in pairs, line by line, and recite it from memory (Task D).
Ss. write two new lines about their favourite healthy food; 3–4 Ss. read their lines to the class.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Grammar (Part 1): the present continuous (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the present continuous in the affirmative, negative and interrogative forms to talk about actions happening now.
lessons.point: Form: am / is / are + verb-ing · Use: an action happening now — now, right now, at the moment, Look!, Listen!

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. mimes cooking and asks: “What am I doing?” Ss. guess: “You're cooking.”
T. shows the two pictures; Ss. read the phone dialogue and answer: “What is Salma doing? What is her dad doing?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the present continuous verbs in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A); pair check.
T. builds the form on the board: am / is / are + verb-ing.
T. asks CCQs: “Is Salma cooking now or every day? (now) Is Ayoub helping in the kitchen? (No, he isn't)”
T. reads the Remember box with the class: time words and spelling (making, cutting, sitting).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. put the verbs in brackets in the present continuous (Task B).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board and highlights the spelling changes.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. look at the clues and write what each person is or isn't doing, then a question and a short answer (Task C).
Ss. ask and answer the questions with a partner; T. checks question order and short answers.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. play “Guess what I'm doing!”: one S. mimes a kitchen action, the partner asks Yes / No questions to guess it (Task D).
Ss. write four sentences about what their family is doing right now and read them to a partner.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Grammar (Part 2): quantifiers & articles (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the quantifiers a few, a little, a lot of, many and much, and the articles a, an, the and no article, to talk about food and quantities.
lessons.point: How many + countable? · How much + uncountable? · a lot of = countable and uncountable

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the pictures and asks: “What can you see in Grandma's kitchen? What can she make with lentils?”
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “What are Grandma and Salma making?” (lentil soup).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the quantifiers in the dialogue, tick the right column and write an example (Task A); pair check.
T. sorts countable / uncountable nouns on the board.
T. asks CCQs: “Can we count tomatoes? (yes) Salt? (no) Why ‘the cumin’? (a specific one) Why no article in ‘Soup is good for you’? (soup in general)”
T. reads the Remember box with the class (a / an / the / Ø, How many / How much).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct quantifier (Task B), then complete the sentences with a, an, the or Ø (Task C).
Ss. check in pairs; T. corrects on the board and asks Ss. to explain each choice.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. look at what is in Grandma's kitchen and write a sentence for each item with a quantifier or an article (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who checks the quantifier and the article; 3 Ss. write theirs on the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. plan the food and drinks for a class picnic in Ifrane with a partner, using the useful language (Task E).
Pairs write their list in sentences and present it to another pair, who asks “How many …? / How much …?”
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 5 — Writing: A recipe (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a simple recipe for a Moroccan dish with a title, a list of ingredients and ordered steps, using imperatives, sequencers and quantifiers.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss. of Grandma Fatima's lentil soup (Grammar lesson) and shows the pictures.
Ss. read the model recipe and answer: “How many ingredients are there? How long does it take?”
Ss. write the number of each part in the boxes of the recipe (Task A). T. checks and highlights the sequencers (First, Then, Next, After that, Finally) and the imperatives.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put the steps for Moroccan mint tea in the right order (Task B); pair check.
Ss. complete the salad steps with a sequencer and a verb from the boxes (Task C), with a comma after each sequencer.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. choose their favourite Moroccan dish and plan the recipe in the outline (Task D): title, serves / time, ingredients, method, tip — notes only.
Ss. turn the notes into short steps with the sentence starters and compare with a partner. T. monitors and helps with food words.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their recipe (60–80 words) in the frame (Task E).
Ss. check their recipe with the checklist and correct it. T. collects the recipes for written feedback.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Vocabulary: Keeping clean, medical care & prevention (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to recognise and use words about personal hygiene, medical care and prevention to talk about what they do to keep clean and healthy.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. mimes washing hands and brushing teeth and asks: “What am I doing? Why is it important?”
Ss. guess the actions and answer.
T. displays the four pictures and elicits what Ss can see.
Ss. read Salma's text and answer the gist question: “How does Salma keep healthy?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the words with their meanings (Task A), then compare answers.
T. checks answers and writes the words on the board in three groups: hygiene / medical care / prevention.
T. checks meaning with CCQs: “Where do you buy medicine? (at the chemist's) Who writes a prescription? (the doctor) Does a vaccine cure or prevent an illness? (prevent)”.
T. drills pronunciation and stress: germs, cough /kɒf/, chemist's /k/, prescription (oOo), temperature (Ooo).

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B).
T. corrects on the board.
Ss. find the eight health words in the word search (Task C) and write them next to the puzzle.
The first S. to finish reads the words aloud and spells two of them.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. classify the twelve words in the table (Task D).
Ss. add one more word of their own to each column, then compare with a partner.
T. elicits Ss' extra words and adds them to the board.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. asks: “What do you and your family do to keep healthy?” and gives an example.
Ss. write four sentences about their family's healthy habits with words from the lesson (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who says one habit they share.
T. gives delayed feedback on spelling and word use.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Functions: Asking about health & asking for help (ECRIF)
lessons.topic: Asking about health & asking for help
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask about someone's health, say how they feel, and ask for help politely using tags (You don't have …, do you?) and Could you …?
lessons.point: Asking for help with a tag: You don't have a tissue, do you? ↘ (falling tone: you think the answer is no, but you ask politely)

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. holds his head and says: “I've got a headache. How are things going with you?”
Ss. answer freely: “Fine, thanks.” / “Not bad.”
T. shows the two pictures and asks: “Where is Ayoub? How does he feel?”
Ss. listen to and read the dialogue, then answer: “What's wrong with Ayoub? Who does he ask for help?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the expressions in the dialogue and write them in the right column (Task A).
T. checks and builds the board: asking about health / saying how you feel / asking for help.
T. explains the Remember box: You don't have …, do you? = a polite request; answers Yes, I do. / Sorry, I don't.
T. drills the falling tone on the tag: “You don't have a tissue, ↘do you?”
Ss. listen to six short exchanges and tick the correct response (Task B).
Ss. listen again to check; T. corrects and reads the tapescript lines aloud.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task C).
Ss. check with a partner and read the mini-dialogues aloud.
T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write a short exchange for each situation (Task D), then practise it with a partner, changing roles.
Two or three pairs act out their exchanges; the class names the expression used.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task E).
Ss. role-play the situation without looking at the dialogue, then swap roles with a new health problem.
Two or three pairs perform for the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*Yes, I have. → Yes, I do. / *don't you? → do you?).

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Reading: From our school magazine (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to read a short magazine article for gist, choose its best title and identify the main idea of each paragraph about healthy habits.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks: “Do you often feel tired at school? What do you do to stay healthy?”
Ss. answer freely.
Ss. look at the four pictures and say what they have in common.
T. pre-teaches germs, spread, skip (breakfast), check-up and prevention with pictures and mime.
Ss. tick what they think the text is about (Task A).

stages.name: During-reading
steps: T. sets a 2-minute limit. Ss. read the text quickly and check their prediction (Task A).
T. asks: “Was your prediction right? Which words helped you?”
Ss. read quickly again and choose the best title (Task B).
T. checks and explains why the other titles are about one detail only.
T. shows how the first sentence of a paragraph gives its main idea.
Ss. write the number of the paragraph for each main idea (Task C), then compare with a partner.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the sentences are true or false, and justify from the text (Task D).
T. corrects; Ss. read the justifying lines aloud.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. choose the most useful tip for them and write two or three sentences explaining why (Task E).
Ss. compare with a partner; volunteers read their answers to the class.
T. lists the class's favourite tips on the board for the Writing lesson.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
