lessons.title: Unit 6 — Grammar Part 1: must, mustn't, don't have to (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use must, mustn't and don't have to to talk about obligation, prohibition and no obligation in rules for a healthy school.
lessons.point: must → obligation ✓ · mustn't → prohibition ✗ (= Don't!) · don't have to → not necessary (you can if you want)

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows a “No smoking” sign and a hand-washing sign and asks: “What do these signs tell us?”
Ss. answer freely.
Ss. look at the pictures, read the dialogue and answer: “When must the club members come? What mustn't they do?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline must, mustn't and don't have to in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
T. checks the table and clarifies meaning with a ✓ / ✗ / ? board: must = necessary; mustn't = not allowed; don't have to = not necessary.
CCQs: “You don't have to wear a white coat. Can you wear one? (Yes) Is it necessary? (No)”.
T. points out the form (must + base verb, doesn't have to) and drills mustn't /ˈmʌsnt/.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. circle the correct answer in the eight sentences (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. write a rule for each idea with must, mustn't or don't have to (Task C).
Ss. compare their rules with a partner and discuss any differences.
T. elicits one rule per idea and corrects the form.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five rules for their class Healthy Life Club poster (Task D).
Volunteers present their rules; the class votes for the best poster.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*must to, *don't must).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Grammar Part 2: Reflexive pronouns (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself …) correctly to talk about looking after themselves and safety at home.
lessons.point: We use a reflexive pronoun when the subject and the object are the same person: I cut myself. I cut me. ✗

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. mimes cutting a finger and putting on a plaster and says: “I cut myself. I put on the plaster myself.”
Ss. say what happened.
Ss. look at the pictures, read the dialogue and answer: “What is the lesson about? Who lives alone?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the reflexive pronouns in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
T. checks the table and clarifies use: subject = object (I cut myself); by myself = alone, without help.
CCQs: “He hurts himself. Who is hurt? (he) I do it myself. Does someone help me? (No)”.
T. highlights -self / -selves and drills the stress on self.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the eight sentences with the correct reflexive pronoun (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. answer the four questions with full sentences (Task C).
Ss. ask a partner the same questions and note his / her answers.
Volunteers report: “Hiba makes her breakfast herself.”

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four safety tips for a “Stay safe at home” leaflet with reflexive pronouns (Task D).
Ss. read their tips to a partner, then a few to the class.
T. gives delayed feedback on common errors (*hisself, *I cut me).

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 6 — Writing: A letter of advice (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a short letter of advice to a friend with a health problem, using should, mustn't and Why don't you …? with the correct layout.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss of Salma's tips from the Reading lesson and asks: “What can you say to a friend who always feels tired?”
Ss. read Salma's letter to Ayoub and answer: “What is Ayoub's problem? How many pieces of advice does Salma give?”
Ss. write the number of each part in the boxes of the letter (Task A); T. checks.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: T. elicits the advice expressions from the letter and the box: should / shouldn't / Why don't you …? / Try to … / must, mustn't.
Ss. match each problem with the best advice (Task B).
Ss. rewrite the four lines with capitals and punctuation (Task C).
T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: Ss. read Hamza's letter and underline his problems.
T. elicits one piece of advice for each problem.
Ss. plan their reply in the table with the sentence starters (Task D).
T. monitors and helps with ideas and language.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their letter of advice to Hamza (60–80 words) in the frame (Task E).
Ss. check their letter with the checklist and correct their mistakes.
T. collects the letters for marking.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Vocabulary: Hobbies, Sports & Games (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words about leisure activities, sports and games with play, go and do, use a dictionary entry (part of speech, plural, synonym, alphabetical order) and replace words with their synonyms.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “What do you do in your free time?” and writes Ss’ ideas on the board.
T. shows the three pictures and Ss. name the activities (chess, swimming, hiking).
Ss. read Ilyas’s text and answer: “What are Salma’s hobbies?” (collecting stamps, reading comics, painting).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the highlighted words with their meanings (Task A), then compare with a partner.
T. checks the answers and drills the stress: HOBby, PAINTing, PAStime.
T. uses the text to build the board: play + games (play football, chess) · go + -ing (go swimming, go hiking) · do + karate / yoga.
CCQs: “Do we say ‘go football’?” (No, play football) · “Chess or swimming: which one is a board game?” (chess)

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with play, go or do (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board and points out does with he / she.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. shows how to read a dictionary entry: word, pronunciation, part of speech, plural, example, synonym.
Ss. answer the dictionary questions and put words in alphabetical order (Task C).
Ss. match each word with its synonym (Task D).
T. checks and Ss. say a sentence with one synonym: “In my spare time, I …”.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write five sentences about their hobbies and free time, using play / go / do and two synonyms (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who finds one thing in common.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on collocations and spelling.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Functions: Describing Past Actions (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask and answer about past actions (What did you do …? Where did you go? Did you …? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn’t.), react to what others say and take notes while listening.
words: What did you do last weekend?
lessons.point: Did you + verb …? → Did you win? — Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. · What / Where did you + verb …?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. tells the class about his weekend: “Last Sunday, I went to the beach. I played football with my son.”
T. shows the two pictures and asks: “What did they do last weekend?”
Ss. listen to Salma and Anas and take notes in the table: when, where, who with (Task A).
Ss. listen a second time and complete what they did and how it was.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen again and put the expressions in the right column (Task B).
T. elicits and builds the board: Asking (What did you do …? Did you …?) / Describing (I played …, We went to …) / Reacting (That sounds fun!).
CCQs: “Is Anas talking about now or the past?” (the past) · “Did you win? — Yes, I did. Can we say ‘Yes, I won’ too?” (yes, but the short answer is ‘Yes, I did.’)
T. reads the Remember box with Ss.: Did + base verb; went, had, won, took, saw; choral and individual drilling of the questions.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the mini-dialogue with the expressions in the box (Task C).
Ss. check with a partner, then two Ss. read the dialogue aloud.
T. corrects on the board and re-drills difficult lines.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models cue 1 with a strong student: “What did you do last Saturday?” — “I watched a basketball match on TV.”
Ss. write and practise a question and an answer for each cue (Task D), then swap roles.
2–3 Ss. perform; the class says which past form they heard.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A and B (Task E). Ss. role-play talking about last weekend without looking at the dialogue.
Ss. change partners and tell a new partner about their weekend.
T. monitors, notes errors (*Did you went?) and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Reading: My Camera, My Best Friend (PDP)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to read a text about a hobby for relevant details, justify answers from the text and work out implied meaning from clues.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. shows an old camera (or a picture) and asks: “Do you take photos? What do you take photos of?”
T. pre-teaches shy, coach, exhibition and visitor with pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the pictures and guess what Salma’s “best friend” is (Task A).

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. read the text quickly and check their guess in Task A.
T. elicits the answer and the words that helped (camera, photos, club).
T. explains how to find relevant details: underline the key word in the sentence, find it in the text, read only that part.
Ss. decide if the sentences are true or false and justify with a line from the text (Task B).
Ss. answer the detail questions (Task C), then compare with a partner.
T. checks answers and Ss. say the paragraph number.
T. models question 1: “The text doesn’t say ‘I’m not shy now’. Which sentence tells us?” (I talked to a lot of visitors).
Ss. read between the lines and answer the questions with clues (Task D).
T. elicits the clues and accepts reasonable answers.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. write 2–3 sentences about a hobby that helps them (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, then 3–4 Ss. share with the class.
T. tells Ss. that Salma’s text will be the model for the writing lesson.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Grammar Part 1: the verb be in the past simple (ECRIF)
lessons.topic: the verb be in the past simple
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the verb be in the past simple (was / were) in affirmative, negative and interrogative sentences and give short answers.
lessons.point: am / is → was · are → were · I / he / she / it → was · you / we / they → were

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Where are you now?” (in class) “Where were you last Sunday?” and writes 2–3 answers on the board.
T. shows the pictures of the chess competition.
Ss. read the dialogue and answer: “Where was Ilyas on Saturday? Was he happy?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline was, were, wasn’t and weren’t in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A).
T. elicits the answers and completes the table on the board.
T. reads the Remember box: am / is → was, are → were; question = was / were first; short answers.
CCQs: “Is the competition now or in the past?” (past) · “Anas and Kawtar … there: was or were?” (were)
T. drills weak /wəz/ in sentences and strong /wɒz/ in short answers.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with was, were, wasn’t or weren’t (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models sentence 1: “Ilyas wasn’t in Fez. — Was Ilyas in Fez last Saturday? — Yes, he was.”
Ss. write the negative, the question and a short answer for each sentence (Task C).
Ss. ask a partner the questions; 2–3 Ss. read their answers aloud.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write three true sentences about last weekend with the starters (Task D).
Ss. ask a partner the useful questions, then report his / her answers: “Anas was at the stadium. He wasn’t at home.”
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on was / were.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Grammar Part 2: Prepositions of place (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to describe where things are with prepositions of place (in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of, between, opposite, above, near) and ask and answer “Where is / are …?”.
lessons.point: in = inside · on = on the surface · under ≠ above · in front of ≠ behind · next to / near = close to

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. hides a pen and asks: “Where is my pen?” Ss. guess; T. shows it: “It’s under the book.”
T. shows the pictures of the games room.
Ss. read Kawtar’s description and answer: “Where are the footballs?” (under the coach’s desk)

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. read again and complete the table with the prepositions (Task A).
T. checks and writes the prepositions on the board.
T. shows the meaning with a box and a ball: in, on, under, behind, in front of, next to, between, above.
T. reads the Remember box. CCQs: “‘between’: how many things?” (two) · “‘opposite’: are the two things facing each other?” (yes)
Ss. repeat the prepositions with the right stress: beHIND, opPOsite, beTWEEN.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the prepositions in the box (Task B).
Ss. check with a partner; T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models: “The board is behind the teacher’s desk.”
Ss. look around the classroom and write a sentence for each thing, using a different preposition each time (Task C).
Ss. read a sentence; the class says if it is true.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. draw their dream hobby room and write 3 sentences about it (Task D).
Ss. describe the room to a partner, who draws it; then they compare the drawings.
T. monitors and gives delayed feedback on prepositions and is / are.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 7 — Writing: A composition about my favourite hobby (Product)
lessons.topic: A composition about my favourite hobby
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a short composition about their favourite hobby with a title, an introduction, a body with reasons and a conclusion, using because, and, but and also.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. asks: “Do you remember Salma? What is her hobby?” (photography, from the reading lesson)
Ss. read Salma’s composition and answer: “Why does Salma like photography?”
Ss. write the number of each part in its box (Task A).
T. checks and draws the plan on the board: title → introduction → when & where → reasons → conclusion.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: T. elicits the connectors from the model (because, also, In conclusion) and gives their use.
Ss. complete the sentences with the connectors in the box (Task B).
Ss. rewrite the sentences with capital letters and punctuation (Task C).
T. corrects on the board: capitals for I, names, cities, days; comma after In conclusion.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. brainstorms hobbies with the class and writes ideas on the board (sports, games, art, collecting …).
Each S. chooses one hobby and says why he / she likes it.
Ss. plan their composition with the sentence starters and write notes (Task D).
T. moves around and helps with ideas and vocabulary.
Ss. turn their notes into sentences and read them to a partner, who checks the plan is complete.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their composition (Task E), 60–80 words.
Ss. check their composition with the checklist and correct their mistakes.
T. collects the compositions to mark with the marking guide.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Vocabulary: Our planet in danger (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words about the greenhouse effect, a clean environment, endangered species and natural phenomena, and common environmental collocations, to talk about protecting the Earth.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows the four pictures and asks: “What can you see? Is our planet in good health?”
Ss. name what they know (beach, smoke, bird, water) and say what the problem is in each picture.
T. presents Salma's poster for the Green Club. Ss. read it once and answer the gist question: “What does Salma ask us to do?” (recycle waste, save water, plant trees).

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the highlighted words with their meanings (Task A), then check with a partner.
T. checks meaning with the pictures and CCQs: “Does an extinct animal exist today? (No) Is a drought about too much water or no water? (no water)”.
T. drills pronunciation and marks the stress on the board: polLUtion, enDANgered, exTINCT, reCYcle; “drought” /aʊ/, “flood” /ʌ/.
Ss. put the twelve words of the box in the right column (Task B); T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the six sentences with words from the box (Task C).
Ss. compare answers; T. calls on individual Ss. to read the sentences aloud and corrects.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. writes “plant trees” on the board and explains a collocation: words that often go together.
Ss. match the verbs with the nouns (Task D); T. checks and drills the collocations.
Ss. write two sentences of their own with two collocations (Task D).
Volunteers read their sentences; T. corrects form and meaning.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four promises to keep our Earth safe with the new words and collocations: “I promise to … / I promise not to …” (Task E).
Ss. read their pledges to a partner and choose the best two; volunteers read them to the class.
T. writes a “Class Green Pledge” on the board and gives feedback on errors.

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Functions: Asking for permission (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask for, give and refuse permission politely (Can I …? / Could I …? / May I …? — Sure, you can. / I'm afraid you can't.), listen for relevant information and pronounce /e/ and /eɪ/ correctly.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks a student: “Can I borrow your pen?” and waits for the answer. T. asks: “What did I ask for?”
Ss. look at the two pictures and predict: “Who is Anas talking to? What does he want?”
Ss. listen to the dialogue for the first time and tick the right answers (Task A). T. checks the predictions.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen again for relevant information: what Anas asks, Yes or No, and why not (Task B). Pair check, then feedback.
Ss. listen a third time and complete the expressions (Task C). T. builds the board: asking / giving / refusing permission.
CCQs: “Is ‘May I …?’ more or less polite than ‘Can I …?’ (more) Do we give a reason when we say no? (yes)”.
Pronunciation: T. models /e/ (yes, help) and /eɪ/ (may, take); Ss. repeat and put the words in the right column (Task D).
T. drills polite rising intonation in “Can I …?”.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the four mini-dialogues with the expressions in the box (Task E).
Ss. check in pairs; open pairs read the mini-dialogues aloud; T. corrects.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. models situation 1 with a strong student.
Ss. write and practise an exchange for each situation, giving a reason when they say no (Task F).
Two or three pairs perform; the class says which expression they used to ask, give or refuse permission.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. gives out role cards A (Green Club member) and B (park guard) (Task G). Ss. prepare quickly, then role-play the visit to Souss-Massa National Park without looking at Task E.
Ss. change roles and act again; a few pairs perform for the class.
T. monitors, notes errors and gives delayed feedback on the board.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Reading: Our Green Saturday (PDP · skimming)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to skim a text to get its main idea and the main idea of each paragraph, and scan it for specific details about a school clean-up day.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: Warm-up: T. asks “Is our beach clean? What do people leave on the beach?”
T. pre-teaches rubbish, shocked, rare, guide and in the wild with the pictures and mime.
Ss. look at the title and the three pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A). T. writes the class predictions on the board.

stages.name: During-reading
steps: T. explains skimming: read quickly, look at the title, the first line of each paragraph and key words.
Ss. skim the text in one minute to check their predictions (Task A).
Ss. skim again and match each paragraph with its main idea (Task B). T. asks: “Which words helped you?”
Ss. choose the main purpose of the text (Task C) and justify with the last sentence of the text.
Ss. read carefully and decide if the statements are true or false, justifying with words from the text (Task D). Pair check; feedback with the paragraph numbers.
Ss. scan the text to answer the detail questions (Task E); volunteers write the answers on the board.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: Ss. write three small actions their class can do to keep our Earth safe (Task F).
Ss. read their actions to a partner; T. collects the best ideas on the board as a class “green list” and Ss. vote for the top three.
T. links the list to the Writing lesson (a paragraph about protecting the environment).

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Grammar Part 1: Past simple of regular verbs (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the past simple of regular verbs in the affirmative, negative and interrogative forms to talk about past actions.
lessons.point: Affirmative: verb + -ed for all persons: I / you / he / she / we / they cleaned.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. reminds Ss. of the Green Club clean-up from the Reading lesson and asks: “When was it? Is it finished?”
Ss. look at the pictures and read the dialogue to answer: “Did Khadija go to the clean-up? Why not?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. look at the highlighted verbs and complete the table (Task A); T. checks on the board.
T. elicits the rule: verb + -ed for all persons; didn't + base verb; Did + subject + base verb?
T. goes through the Remember box: spelling rules (+d, y → ied, double consonant) and the common error “didn't stayed”.
CCQs: “Do we use -ed after didn't? (No) Is ‘Did you visit …?’ about now or the past? (the past)”.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. write the past form of the eight verbs using the spelling rules (Task B).
Ss. complete Hajar's diary with the past simple, affirmative or negative (Task C); Ss. compare, then T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. write questions and short answers from the cues (Task D).
Ss. ask and answer the questions with a partner; T. checks the form Did + subject + base verb and the short answers.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Find someone who …”: Ss. walk around and ask “Did you … last weekend?” and write a classmate's name for each action (Task E).
Ss. write three sentences about their classmates (Task E); volunteers read them.
T. gives feedback on common errors on the board.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Grammar Part 2: Question tags (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to form and use question tags with be, can and do / does / did to check information or ask for agreement.
lessons.point: Positive statement → negative tag: It is beautiful, isn't it? · Negative statement → positive tag: You don't recycle, do you?

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. says: “You did your homework, didn't you?” and waits for answers; Ss. guess what T. wants (to check).
Ss. look at the pictures and read the dialogue to answer: “What are Salma and Anas preparing?” (a poster for the Green Club exhibition)

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the question tags in the dialogue, decide if each statement is positive or negative and complete the table (Task A).
T. elicits the rule with the Remember box: positive statement → negative tag, negative statement → positive tag, same auxiliary + pronoun.
T. models and drills falling (checking) and rising (real question) intonation.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. match the statements with the question tags (Task B).
Ss. add the correct tag to the six sentences (Task C); pair check, then T. corrects on the board.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. write a sentence with a question tag from each cue (Task D).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who answers “Yes, …” or “No, …”; T. checks the auxiliaries and pronouns.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: “Guess and check”: Ss. write four sentences with tags about their partner and the environment (Task E).
Ss. check with their partner using falling intonation and tick the right guesses; the pair with the most ticks wins.
T. gives delayed feedback on errors.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 8 — Writing: Coherent paragraphs (Product approach)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a coherent paragraph with a topic sentence, supporting ideas, connectors and a concluding sentence about protecting the environment at school.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. reminds Ss. of their “green list” from the Reading lesson and asks: “How can we keep our town clean?”
Ss. read Anas's paragraph and say how many ideas he gives (four).
Ss. label the boxes of the paragraph T, S or C (Task A). T. explains: one main idea, a topic sentence, supporting sentences, a concluding sentence and connectors (underlined).

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. put Khadija's paragraph about saving water in the right order (Task B) and say which words helped them (connectors).
Ss. complete the sentences with connectors from the box (Task C); T. corrects and adds the connectors to the board.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. writes the topic on the board: “How can students protect the environment at school?” Ss. brainstorm ideas together.
Ss. plan their paragraph in the outline using the sentence starters: topic sentence, three ideas, an example, a reason and a concluding sentence (Task D).
T. monitors and helps with ideas and vocabulary.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their paragraph (60–80 words) with a title (Task E).
Ss. check their paragraph with the checklist, then swap with a partner who ticks the checklist too.
T. collects the paragraphs for marking with the guide.

lessons.label: Vocabulary
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Vocabulary: Jobs, Money & Services (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use words related to (un)employment, the economy, services and money, find antonyms and use a dictionary entry to check meaning, part of speech, pronunciation and opposites.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows a 200-dirham banknote and some coins and asks: “What can you buy with this? Where do people get money?”
Ss. look at the three pictures and say what they see (a cake shop, coins and banknotes, a bank).
Ss. read Kawtar's text twice and answer the gist question: “What was Kawtar's problem three years ago? What is her job now?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. match the six words with their meanings (Task A); pair check; T. elicits and confirms.
T. builds a board table: Money (cash, coins, banknotes, salary, earn, loan, savings account) · Jobs (job, unemployed, customer) · Services (bank, post office, ATM).
T. shows the word parts un- + employ + -ed and checks meaning with CCQs: “If you borrow money, do you give it or take it?”
Pronunciation: salary, unemployed, economy, customer — choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the words in the box (Task B); T. corrects on the board.
Ss. match each word with its opposite (Task C); T. checks and drills the pairs: rich ≠ poor, spend ≠ save, borrow ≠ lend …

stages.name: Internalize
steps: T. projects the dictionary entry for “save” and elicits its parts: headword, pronunciation, part of speech, meaning, example, opposite.
Ss. answer the questions about the entry (Task D).
Ss. put the six words in alphabetical order (Task E); T. shows what to do when two words begin with the same letter (cash / customer).

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write four sentences about money in their life, each with a pair of opposites (Task F).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who finds the pair of opposites. T. gives delayed feedback on word choice (lend / borrow, earn / win).

lessons.label: Functions
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Functions: Asking about & expressing ability (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to ask about ability and express ability and inability (Can you …? / I can … very well. / No, I can't.) in a job interview, after listening for details.
lessons.point: can + verb: She can speak English. ✓ She cans speak ✗ She can to speak ✗ · Question: Can you drive? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Remember Kawtar? Her shop is busy now. What does she need?” (a shop assistant).
Ss. look at the pictures and read the job offer: “What job is it? What questions are in the advert?”
Ss. listen for the first time and tick the right answers (Task A); pair check; T. confirms.

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. listen again and write ✓ or ✗ for Rachid and Salma, plus one detail (Task B); T. checks with the class.
Ss. put the expressions in the right column (Task C); T. checks and writes the three columns on the board.
T. clarifies the form with the Remember box: can + base verb, no “to”, no “-s”. CCQ: “Can we say ‘She cans swim’?” (No)
Pronunciation: weak /kən/ in “I can swim”, strong /kæn/ in “Yes, I can”, long /kɑːnt/ in “can't” — choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete Hind's interview with the words in the box (Task D); pair check.
Two pairs read the mini-dialogue aloud; T. corrects the pronunciation of can / can't.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. write short exchanges from the cues (Task E), using their own ideas.
Ss. read their exchanges to a partner; T. elicits some answers and corrects the form.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: T. models the job-interview role-play with a volunteer (Task F).
Ss. read their role cards and act out the interview, then change roles.
Two pairs perform; the class says if the candidate gets the job. T. gives delayed feedback on can / can't and short answers.

lessons.label: Reading
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Reading: From Job Seeker to Shop Owner (PDP)
lessons.topic: From Job Seeker to Shop Owner
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to guess the meaning of unfamiliar words from context, using the words around them, part of speech, word parts and contrast words, in a text about a young Moroccan business owner.

stages.name: Pre-reading
steps: T. asks: “What can people do when they lose their job?” and writes Ss' ideas on the board.
Ss. look at the title and the three pictures and predict what the text is about (Task A). T. writes the predictions on the board.
T. tells Ss: “There are new words in bold. Don't use a dictionary: today we guess!”

stages.name: During-reading
steps: Ss. read the text quickly and check their prediction (Task A); T. confirms and asks: “Is Kawtar's story happy or sad?”
Ss. read again and answer True / False, justifying from the text (Task B); pair check; T. corrects.
Ss. find the words that match the meanings, using the paragraph numbers (Task C); T. elicits and asks: “How did you find it?”
T. presents the four clues in the box: words around it, part of speech, word parts, opposites / contrast words.
Ss. guess the meaning of the three words in bold and say which clue helped them (Task D); T. checks and shows how each clue works.

stages.name: Post-reading
steps: T. reads Kawtar's quote and asks: “Do you agree? What small business would you like to start in your town?”
Ss. write their view in 3–4 sentences (Task E), then read them to a partner.
Some Ss. read their ideas to the class; T. gives feedback and tells Ss that the next lessons continue Kawtar's story.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 1
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Grammar Part 1: Past simple of irregular verbs (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to use the past simple of irregular verbs in the affirmative, negative and interrogative, and pronounce the -ed ending of regular verbs correctly (/t/, /d/, /ɪd/).
lessons.point: ✓ Kawtar went to the bank. (same form for all persons: I / you / he / she / we / they went)

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. asks: “Remember Kawtar from the Reading lesson? What did she do three years ago?” and writes Ss' answers on the board.
Ss. look at the pictures and read Hiba's interview with Kawtar.
Ss. answer the gist questions: “How did Kawtar get the money? Did she sell many cakes at first?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. underline the verbs in the past and complete the table of irregular verbs (Task A); T. checks on the board.
T. elicits the rule with the Remember box: affirmative (same form for all persons), negative (didn't + base verb), questions and short answers (Did … ? — Yes, I did.).
CCQs: “After didn't, do we say had or have?” (have) · “Do irregular verbs take -ed?” (no)
T. reviews the -ed sounds with worked /t/, opened /d/, wanted /ɪd/; choral and individual drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the past simple of the verbs in brackets (Task B); pair check; T. corrects.
Ss. put the regular verbs in the right column /t/, /d/, /ɪd/ (Task C) and say them aloud.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. make each sentence negative, then write a question and a short answer (Task D).
Ss. ask and answer the questions with a partner; T. elicits answers and corrects the form.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: Ss. write three true sentences about what they did with their money last month (Task E).
Ss. read their sentences to a partner, who asks follow-up questions: “Did you …? What did you buy? How much did you spend?”
Some Ss. report one thing about their partner; T. gives delayed feedback on did + base verb and -ed sounds.

lessons.label: Grammar - Part 2
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Grammar Part 2: Superlatives (ECRIF)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to compare three or more things using superlatives of short, long and irregular adjectives (the strongest, the most serious, the best).
lessons.point: short: strong → the strongest · nice → the nicest · big → the biggest · easy → the easiest

stages.name: Encounter
steps: T. shows three prices on the board (6 DH, 7.50 DH, 9 DH) and asks: “Which is cheaper? Which one is the cheapest?”
Ss. look at the pictures and read the dialogue between Kawtar and Imane.
Ss. answer: “Which supplier do they choose? Why?”

stages.name: Clarify
steps: Ss. find the superlatives in the dialogue and complete the table (Task A); T. checks on the board.
T. elicits the rules with the Remember box: short adjectives (+ -est, double consonant, y → -iest), long adjectives (the most + adjective), irregular (the best, the worst, the farthest).
CCQs: “Atlas is the cheapest. Is there a cheaper supplier?” (no) · “How many things do we compare?” (three or more)
Pronunciation: the cheapest /ðə ˈtʃiːpɪst/ — choral drilling.

stages.name: Remember
steps: Ss. complete the sentences with the superlative of the adjectives in brackets (Task B); pair check.
T. corrects on the board and focuses on “the”: *Casablanca is biggest city → the biggest.

stages.name: Internalize
steps: Ss. read the table about the three phones and write sentences with superlatives (Task C).
Ss. compare their sentences with a partner; T. elicits one sentence for each adjective.

stages.name: Fluently Use
steps: In groups, Ss. ask the questions in the box about money records in the class (Task D) and take notes.
Ss. write three sentences about their group.
One S. from each group reads the results; T. gives delayed feedback on the form.

lessons.label: Writing
lessons.title: Unit 9 — Writing: A story (Product)
lessons.objective: By the end of the lesson, students will be able to write a short story about a lucky day, with a title, a setting, a problem, events in order and an ending, using the past simple, sequencers and correct punctuation.

stages.name: Model / Familiarization
steps: T. shows the two pictures and asks: “What did the boy find? What can you do when you find money in the street?”
Ss. read the model story and answer: “What did Anas find? What did he do?”
Ss. write the numbers of the six story parts in the boxes (Task A); T. checks and highlights the sequencers (First, Then, After that, Finally) and the past simple verbs.

stages.name: Controlled Practice
steps: Ss. complete Hind's story with the sequencers (Task B); pair check.
Ss. rewrite the sentences with capital letters, commas, speech marks and question marks (Task C); T. shows the rule: “Thank you,” said Mr. Tazi.

stages.name: Guided Writing
steps: T. presents the task: “A lucky day: a person finds, loses or wins some money.” Ss. brainstorm ideas with a partner.
Ss. plan their story in the outline (Task D) with the sentence starters: setting · problem · events · ending · lesson — notes only.
Ss. tell their plan to a partner, who asks one question: “Where was she? What did he do next?” T. monitors and helps.

stages.name: Free Writing
steps: Ss. write their story (60–80 words) in the writing frame (Task E).
Ss. check their story with the self-check checklist and correct it. T. collects the stories for written feedback.
